sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶

translations.literal: = Zheng Yuqing =
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶，字居業，鄭州滎陽人，三世皆顯宦。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuqing, courtesy name Juye, was a man of Xingyang in Zheng prefecture; for three generations his family had held prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing, styled Juye, came from Xingyang in Zheng prefecture. For three generations his line had held high office.

sentences.zh: 餘慶少善屬文，擢進士第。

translations.literal: In youth Yuqing was skilled at literary composition and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Yuqing excelled at prose and won the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 嚴震帥山南西道，奏置幕府。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhen commanded the Shannan West Circuit, he memorialized to place Yuqing on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhen was military governor of Shannan West, he had Yuqing appointed to his staff.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，還朝，擢庫部郎中，為翰林學士，以工部侍郎知吏部選。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he returned to court, was promoted to director of the Bureau of Revenues, became a Hanlin academician, and as vice minister of works oversaw the Ministry of Personnel's selections.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he came back to the capital, rose to director of the Bureau of Revenues, entered the Hanlin Academy, and as vice minister of works supervised civil-service appointments.

sentences.zh: 浮屠法湊以罪為民訴闕下，詔御史中丞宇文邈、刑部侍郎張彧、大理卿鄭雲逵為三司，與功德判官諸葛述參按。

translations.literal: The monk Fa Cou was accused by the people at the palace gates; the throne ordered Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Miao, Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Yu, and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Zheng Yunkui to form a three-office tribunal, with Merit Commissioner judge Zhuge Shu to assist in the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist monk Fa Cou was charged by common petitioners at court. The emperor appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Miao, Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Yu, and Chief Judge Zheng Yunkui as a joint tribunal, with Merit Commissioner judge Zhuge Shu to assist the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 述，故史也，餘慶劾述猥賤，不宜與三司雜治，時韙其言。

translations.literal: Shu was a former clerk; Yuqing impeached him as base and mean, unfit to sit with the three offices in a joint trial, and at the time people approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had once been a clerk. Yuqing charged that he was too low and contemptible to sit with the three high officers on the same case, and opinion at the time sided with him.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he was appointed vice secretary of the Secretariat and Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 14 he was made vice secretary of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 每奏對，多傅經義。

translations.literal: Whenever he answered memorials at audience, he often expounded the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he often grounded his replies in classical doctrine.

sentences.zh: 素善度支使於䪹，凡所陳，必左右之，䪹坐事貶；

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Revenue Commissioner Yu Di; whatever Di proposed, Yuqing always supported him, and Di was demoted for an offense;
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Revenue Commissioner Yu Di and always backed his proposals. Di was later demoted for misconduct;

sentences.zh: 又歲旱饑，朝廷議賑禁衛十軍，為中書史漏言。

translations.literal: moreover, in a year of drought and famine the court debated relief for the ten metropolitan guard armies, and a Secretariat clerk leaked the discussion.
translations.idiomatic: and when drought and famine struck, the court debated famine relief for the ten metropolitan guard armies—a plan a Secretariat clerk leaked.

sentences.zh: 疊二忤，故貶郴州司馬。

translations.literal: With these two offenses piled together, he was therefore demoted to aide of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With both offenses against him, he was demoted to aide of Chen.

sentences.zh: 順宗以尚書左丞召，會憲宗立，即其官復拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Emperor Shunzong summoned him as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs; when Emperor Xianzong acceded, he was at once reappointed chief minister in that same office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shunzong recalled him as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs. When Xianzong took the throne, he was immediately reappointed chief minister in that post.

sentences.zh: 時主書滑渙與宦人劉光琦相倚為奸，每宰相議，為光琦沮變者，令渙往請必得，由是四方貲餉奔委之，弟泳至官刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Clerk Hua Huan and the eunuch Liu Guangqi relied on each other in villainy; whenever the chief ministers deliberated and Guangqi blocked a decision, Huan would be sent to petition and always got his way, so gifts and bribes from all quarters poured in on them, and Huan's younger brother Yong rose to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Hua Huan and the eunuch Liu Guangqi then worked corruption together. When councilors debated a matter Guangqi wished to overturn, Huan would be sent to lobby and always prevailed. Gifts from every quarter flooded in on them, and Huan's brother Yong became a prefect.

sentences.zh: 杜佑、鄭絪執政，頗姑息，而佑常行輩待，不名也。

translations.literal: Du You and Zheng Yin held power and were quite indulgent; You moreover treated Yuqing by seniority alone and would not call him by name.
translations.idiomatic: Du You and Zheng Yin governed with lax indulgence. You in particular treated Yuqing only as a junior colleague and never addressed him by name.

sentences.zh: 至餘慶議事，渙傲然指畫諸宰相前，餘慶叱去。

translations.literal: When Yuqing came to deliberate, Huan would arrogantly gesture and instruct before all the chief ministers; Yuqing shouted him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqing joined deliberations, Huan would stand before the chief ministers and arrogantly direct affairs. Yuqing drove him out with a rebuke.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: Before long he was removed and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was dismissed from the council and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 後渙以贓敗，帝浸聞叱去事，善之。

translations.literal: Later Huan was ruined for bribery; the emperor gradually heard of the rebuke and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan later fell to a bribery scandal, the emperor gradually learned of Yuqing's rebuke and commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 改國子祭酒，累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of the National University and eventually promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chancellor of the National University and later rose to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 醫工崔環者，自淮南小將除黃州司馬，餘慶執奏：「諸道散將無功受五品正員，開僥幸路，不可。」

translations.literal: A medical officer named Cui Huan, a former junior officer in Huainan, was appointed aide of Huang prefecture; Yuqing firmly memorialized: "Dispersed officers from the circuits who receive fifth-rank regular posts without merit open a path of favoritism—this must not be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: A medical officer named Cui Huan, formerly a junior officer in Huainan, was appointed aide of Huang. Yuqing firmly protested: "Dispersed officers from the provinces who receive regular fifth-rank posts without merit open the door to favoritism. This cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 權者不悅，改太子少傅，兼判太常卿事。

translations.literal: The powerful were displeased; he was transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently acted as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful were displeased. He was made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently supervised the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 自朱泚亂，都輦數驚，太常肄樂禁用鼓，餘慶以時久平，奏復舊制。

translations.literal: Since Zhu Ci's rebellion the capital had been repeatedly alarmed, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, when rehearsing music, had forbidden drums; Yuqing, because peace had long returned, memorialized to restore the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhu Ci's rebellion the capital had been repeatedly alarmed, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had banned drums in musical rehearsals. Yuqing, holding that peace had long been restored, memorialized to revive the old practice.

sentences.zh: 出為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: He went out as military governor of the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military governor of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 入拜太子少師，請老，不許。

translations.literal: He entered court as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and asked to retire on account of age; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, he asked to retire. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時數赦，官多泛階；

translations.literal: At the time amnesties were frequent and officials widely received blanket promotions in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Amnesties were frequent and officials were widely promoted in rank without cause;

sentences.zh: 又帝親郊，陪祠者授三品、五品，不計考；

translations.literal: moreover, when the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice, those attending the rites were given third- and fifth-rank posts without regard to merit review;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor performed the suburban sacrifice in person, attendants were given third- and fifth-rank posts with no merit review;

sentences.zh: 使府賓吏，以軍功借賜朱紫率十八；

translations.literal: guests and clerks of commissioner envoys, on pretext of military merit, were lent purple and scarlet robes at a rate of eighteen in ten;
translations.idiomatic: envoys' staff were lent purple and scarlet insignia on pretext of military merit at a rate of roughly eighteen in ten;

sentences.zh: 近臣謝、郎官出使，多所賜與；

translations.literal: favored ministers on leave and bureau officials sent on missions received many such gifts;
translations.idiomatic: favored ministers on leave and bureau officials on mission received lavish grants;

sentences.zh: 每朝會，朱紫滿廷而少衣綠者。

translations.literal: at every court assembly the hall was full of scarlet and purple while few wore green.
translations.idiomatic: at every court assembly scarlet and purple filled the hall while green-robed officials were few.

sentences.zh: 品服太濫，人不以為貴，帝亦惡之，始詔餘慶條奏懲革。

translations.literal: Rank and insignia were so abused that people no longer held them in esteem; the emperor too detested this and first ordered Yuqing to submit detailed proposals for punishment and reform.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and dress had become so cheap that they no longer commanded respect. The emperor detested this as well and ordered Yuqing to draft reforms.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 僕射比非其人，及餘慶以宿德進，公論浩然歸重。

translations.literal: The vice directorship had lately not been held by worthy men; when Yuqing advanced on the strength of long-standing virtue, public opinion wholeheartedly turned to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Recent appointees to the vice directorship had not been worthy men. When Yuqing rose on long-standing virtue, public opinion rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 帝患典制不倫，謂餘慶淹該前載，乃詔為詳定使，俾參裁訂正。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that ritual regulations were disorderly and, deeming Yuqing broadly versed in earlier records, appointed him commissioner for detailed revision to assist in adjudicating corrections.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found court ritual in disarray. Judging Yuqing broadly versed in precedent, he appointed him commissioner for detailed revision of ceremonial law.

sentences.zh: 餘慶引韓愈、李程為副，崔郾、陳佩、楊嗣復、庾敬休為判官，凡損增儀矩，號稱詳衷。

translations.literal: Yuqing brought in Han Yu and Li Cheng as deputies, with Cui Yan, Chen Pei, Yang Sifu, and Yu Jingxiu as judges; all additions and reductions to ceremonial rules were praised as thorough and sound.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing named Han Yu and Li Cheng as deputies and Cui Yan, Chen Pei, Yang Sifu, and Yu Jingxiu as reviewers. Their revisions to ritual were hailed as thorough and judicious.

sentences.zh: 俄拜鳳翔尹，節度鳳翔。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Fengxiang and military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect and military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 復為太子少師，封滎陽郡公，兼判國子祭酒事。

translations.literal: He again became Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang commandery, and concurrently supervised the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed Duke of Xingyang, and concurrently supervised the National University.

sentences.zh: 建言：「兵興以來，學校廢，諸生離散。

translations.literal: He offered advice: "Since the wars began the schools have been abandoned and the students scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed: "Since the wars began the schools have fallen into ruin and the students have scattered.

sentences.zh: 今天下承平，臣願率文吏月俸百取一，以資完葺。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is at peace; your servant wishes to lead civil officials in giving one part in a hundred of their monthly salaries to fund repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is at peace, I ask to lead civil officials in contributing one percent of our monthly salaries toward restoration.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，加檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Yuqing was given the honorary title of Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Yuqing was given the honorary rank of Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五，贈太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-five; posthumously he was given Grand Mentor and the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five. Posthumously he was made Grand Mentor with the posthumous name Zhen, meaning Upright.

sentences.zh: 帝以其貧，特給一月奉料為赗禭。

translations.literal: Because he was poor, the emperor specially granted one month's salary as funeral offering.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had died poor, the emperor granted one month's salary for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 餘慶少砥礪，行己完潔。

translations.literal: In youth Yuqing disciplined himself and kept his conduct pure and complete.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuqing disciplined himself and lived with scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 仕四朝，其祿悉赒所親，或濟人急，而自奉粗狹。

translations.literal: Serving four reigns, he gave all his salary to kin, or relieved others in distress, while his own living was coarse and spare.
translations.idiomatic: Through four reigns he gave his entire salary to relatives or to those in urgent need, while he himself lived plainly.

sentences.zh: 至官府，乃開肆廣大，常語人曰：「祿不及親友而侈仆妾者，吾鄙之。」

translations.literal: Only when he reached office did he open his establishment wide; he often told people: "Those who do not share salary with kin and friends yet lavish it on servants and concubines—I despise them.
translations.idiomatic: Only in office did he keep a spacious establishment. He often said: "I despise men who lavish salary on servants and concubines but do not share it with kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 大抵中外姻嫁，其禮獻皆親閱之。

translations.literal: In general, for marriages within and outside the clan, he personally inspected all ritual gifts.
translations.idiomatic: For marriages within and outside the clan he personally reviewed every ceremonial gift.

sentences.zh: 後生內謁，必引見，諄諄教以經義，務成就儒學。

translations.literal: When younger men called privately, he always received them and earnestly taught them the meaning of the classics, striving to complete their Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Young men who visited him privately were always received and earnestly instructed in the classics, that they might complete their Confucian training.

sentences.zh: 自至德後，方鎮除拜，必遣內使持幢節就第，至則多饋金帛，且以媚天子，唯恐不厚，故一使者納至數百萬緡。

translations.literal: Since the Zhide era, when frontier commissioners were appointed, palace envoys bearing banners and credentials were always sent to their homes; on arrival they received large gifts of gold and silk, flattering the Son of Heaven and fearing to give too little, so that a single envoy might collect several million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhide era, when military governors were appointed, palace envoys bearing banners and credentials were sent to their homes. Governors showered them with gold and silk to curry favor with the throne, and a single envoy might collect millions of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 憲宗每命餘慶，必誡使曰：「是家貧，不可妄求取。」

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Xianzong appointed Yuqing, he always warned the envoy: "That household is poor; do not demand gifts recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xianzong appointed Yuqing, he warned the envoy: "That household is poor. Do not demand gifts from them.

sentences.zh: 議者或詆其沽激，餘慶不屑也。

translations.literal: Some critics slandered him as posturing for reputation; Yuqing paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Some critics called him a poseur. Yuqing ignored them.

sentences.zh: 奏議類用古言，如「仰給縣官」、「馬萬蹄」，有司不曉何等語，人訾其不適時。

translations.literal: His memorials often used archaic language, such as "relying on county provision" and "ten thousand horse hooves"; the offices did not understand what such phrases meant, and people criticized him as ill-suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials often used archaic phrases such as "relying on county provision" and "ten thousand horse hooves." The bureaus could not make sense of them, and critics said he was out of step with the age.

sentences.zh: 與從父絪家昭國坊，絪第在南，餘慶第在北，世謂「南鄭相」、「北鄭相」云。

translations.literal: He and his father's younger cousin Yin had homes in Zhaoguo ward; Yin's residence was on the south and Yuqing's on the north, so the age called them "the southern Zheng chief minister" and "the northern Zheng chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: He and his cousin Zheng Yin both lived in Zhaoguo ward—Yin to the south and Yuqing to the north—whence people spoke of "the southern Zheng minister" and "the northern Zheng minister."

sentences.zh: 子澣。

translations.literal: His son Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Huan.

sentences.zh: 澣本名涵，避文宗故名，改焉。

translations.literal: Huan's original name was Han; to avoid the taboo on Emperor Wenzong's name he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had originally been named Han; he changed the name to avoid the taboo on Emperor Wenzong's given name.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累遷右補闕。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was promoted in succession to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose to Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 敢言，無所諱，憲宗謂餘慶曰：「涵，卿令子而朕直臣也，可更相賀。」

translations.literal: He spoke boldly without reserve; Emperor Xianzong told Yuqing: "Han is your fine son and my forthright minister—we may congratulate each other.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke boldly and held nothing back. Xianzong told Yuqing: "Han is your worthy son and my outspoken minister. We may congratulate each other.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人、考功員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist of Attendance and Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Diarist of Attendance and vice director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 時刺史或迫吏下紀功愛，涵請責觀察使以杜其欺。

translations.literal: At the time some prefects forced subordinates to record inflated merit and favor; Han asked that the observation commissioners be held responsible to stop such fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Some prefects then forced clerks to inflate merit records. Han asked that observation commissioners be held accountable to stop the fraud.

sentences.zh: 餘慶為僕射，避除國子博士、史館脩撰。

translations.literal: When Yuqing became vice director, Huan withdrew to avoid conflict and was appointed Erudite of the National University and Compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqing became vice director, Huan stepped aside and was appointed erudite of the National University and compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，入翰林為侍講學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong acceded, Huan entered the Hanlin as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong took the throne, Huan entered the Hanlin as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝使稡擷經史為《要錄》，愛其博而精，試舉諸條擿問之，隨即酬析，無留答，因賜金紫服。

translations.literal: The emperor had him compile selections from the classics and histories into 《Essential Records》; pleased with its breadth and precision, he tested him by picking entries at random to question him; Huan answered at once without hesitation and was therefore granted gold and purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him compile selections from the classics and histories into the "Essential Records." Delighted with its breadth and precision, he quizzed him on random entries; Huan answered instantly without pause and was granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 累進尚書左丞，出為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and went out as military governor of the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and was sent out as military governor of Shannan West.

sentences.zh: 始，餘慶在興元創學廬，澣嗣完之，養生徒，風化大行。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuqing had founded a school lodge at Xingyuan; Huan completed what he had begun, nurtured the students, and moral transformation flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing had earlier founded a school at Xingyuan; Huan finished the work, supported the students, and moral influence spread widely.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書召，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Revenue but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of Revenue but died before he could assume the post.

sentences.zh: 年六十四，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: He was sixty-four; posthumously he was given Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-four. Posthumously he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous name Xuan, meaning Illustrious.

sentences.zh: 四子，處誨、從讜尤知名。

translations.literal: He had four sons; Chuhui and Congzan were especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons; Chuhui and Congzan were especially well known.

sentences.zh: 子 處誨處誨，字廷美，文辭秀拔。

translations.literal: Son Chuhui—Chuhui, courtesy name Tingmei, was outstanding in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuhui, styled Tingmei, was distinguished for elegant prose.

sentences.zh: 仕歷刑部侍郎、浙東觀察、宣武節度使，卒。

translations.literal: In office he served as Vice Minister of Justice, Zhedong observation commissioner, and military governor of Xuanwu, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice minister of justice, Zhedong observation commissioner, and military governor of Xuanwu, then died.

sentences.zh: 先是，李德裕《次柳氏舊聞》，處誨謂未詳，更撰《明皇雜錄》，為時盛傳。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Deyu had compiled 《Sequel to the Liu Family Old Tales》; Chuhui held it insufficiently detailed and wrote anew 《Miscellaneous Records of Emperor Ming》, which was widely circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had earlier compiled the "Sequel to the Liu Family Old Tales." Chuhui found it incomplete and wrote 《Miscellaneous Records of Emperor Ming》, which became widely read.

sentences.zh: 子 從讜從讜，字正求。

translations.literal: Son Congzan—Congzan, courtesy name Zhengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congzan, styled Zhengqiu.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，補校書郎，遷累左補闕。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, and was promoted in succession to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, became a collator, and rose to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 令狐、魏扶皆澣門生，數進譽之，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Linghu and Wei Fu were both Huan's students; they repeatedly praised him to the throne, and he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tao and Wei Fu, both Huan's students, repeatedly commended him at court, and he was made Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，為吏部侍郎，銓次明允。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era he was Vice Minister of Personnel; his ranking of candidates was clear and fair.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiantong he was vice minister of personnel and conducted selections with clarity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 出為河東節度使，徙宣武，以善最聞。

translations.literal: He went out as military governor of Hedong, was transferred to Xuanwu, and was known for outstanding merit ratings.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military governor of Hedong, transferred to Xuanwu, and earned a reputation for excellent administration.

sentences.zh: 改嶺南東道節度。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Lingnan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Lingnan East.

sentences.zh: 先是，林邑蠻內侵，召天下兵進援，會龐勛亂，不復遣，而北兵寡弱。

translations.literal: Earlier the Linyi barbarians had invaded inward; troops from all the realm were summoned to aid, but when Pang Xun's rebellion broke out they were no longer sent, and the northern garrison was few and weak.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Linyi had earlier raided the frontier and troops from across the empire were summoned to help. Pang Xun's rebellion then halted further reinforcements, leaving the northern garrison thin and weak.

sentences.zh: 從讜募土豪，署其酋右職，為約束，使相捍禦，交、廣晏然。

translations.literal: Congzan recruited local strongmen, appointed their chiefs to honorary posts, set regulations, and had them defend one another; Jiaozhi and Guangzhou were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan recruited local magnates, gave their leaders honorary posts under strict rules, and had them defend one another. Jiaozhi and Guangzhou remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong acceded, Congzan was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong took the throne, Congzan was recalled as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢同中書門下平章事，進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery and advanced to Vice Secretary of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was made chief minister and promoted to vice secretary of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 沙陀都督李國昌間邊多虞，入據振武、雲朔等州，南略太谷。

translations.literal: The Shatuo commissioner Li Guochang, taking advantage of many alarms on the frontier, entered and seized Zhenwu, Yunshuo, and other prefectures, and raided south toward Taigu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo commissioner Li Guochang exploited frontier unrest to seize Zhenwu, Yunshuo, and other prefectures and raided south toward Taigu.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使康傳圭遣大將伊釗、張彥球、蘇弘軫引兵拒之，戰數負，傳圭斬軫以徇。

translations.literal: The Hedong military governor Kang Chuangu sent his great generals Yi Zhao, Zhang Yanqiu, and Su Hongzhen to lead troops against them; after several defeats Chuangu executed Hongzhen as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong governor Kang Chuangu sent his generals Yi Zhao, Zhang Yanqiu, and Su Hongzhen against them. After repeated defeats Chuangu executed Hongzhen as an example.

sentences.zh: 彥球所部反，攻傳圭，殺之，劫府庫為亂。

translations.literal: Yanqiu's troops mutinied, attacked Chuangu, killed him, and plundered the prefectural treasury in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu's troops mutinied, killed Chuangu, and looted the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以為憂，帝欲大臣臨制，乃拜從讜檢校司徒，以宰相秩復為河東節度，兼行營招討使，詔自擇參佐。

translations.literal: The court was deeply worried; the emperor wished a chief minister to take command in person, and therefore appointed Congzan honorary Defender-in-Chief, restored him as Hedong military governor at chief-minister rank, and concurrently made him campaign pacification commissioner, ordering him to choose his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed. The emperor wanted a senior minister on the scene and appointed Congzan honorary Defender-in-Chief, restored him as Hedong governor at chief-minister rank, and made him campaign pacification commissioner with authority to choose his own staff.

sentences.zh: 從讜即表長安令王調自副，兵部員外郎劉崇龜、司勛員外郎趙崇為節度觀察府判官，前進士劉崇魯推官，左拾遺李渥掌書記，長安尉崔澤支使，皆一時選。

translations.literal: Congzan at once memorialized that Chang'an magistrate Wang Tiao serve as his deputy, with Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Liu Chonggui and Vice Director of the Bureau of Merits Zhao Chong as judges of the military governorship and observation office, former jinshi Liu Chonglu as investigating officer, Left Reminder Li Wo as secretary, and Chang'an sheriff Cui Ze as administrative aide—all men chosen from the finest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan immediately named Chang'an magistrate Wang Tiao as deputy, Liu Chonggui and Zhao Chong as staff judges, former jinshi Liu Chonglu as investigating officer, Left Reminder Li Wo as secretary, and Chang'an sheriff Cui Ze as administrative aide—all outstanding men of the day.

sentences.zh: 京師士人比太原為小朝廷，言得才多也。

translations.literal: Capital scholars compared Taiyuan to a minor court, saying he had gathered many talents.
translations.idiomatic: Men at court compared Taiyuan to a minor court, saying he had assembled exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 時承軍亂，剽奪日旁午。

translations.literal: At the time, in the wake of the army mutiny, looting occurred day after day without pause.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the mutiny, looting went on without cease.

sentences.zh: 從讜既視事，奸無庾情，乃推捕反賊，誅其首惡。

translations.literal: Once Congzan assumed office, no villainy escaped concealment; he pursued and arrested the mutineers and executed the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Once Congzan took office, no wrongdoing escaped him. He hunted down the mutineers and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 以彥球本善意，且才可任，釋不問，而付以兵，曠無余猜，故得其死力。

translations.literal: Because Yanqiu had originally acted in good faith and his talent could still be employed, Congzan released him without punishment and entrusted him with troops, showing no further suspicion, and thus won his utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that Yanqiu had acted in good faith and was still capable, Congzan pardoned him and gave him command without further suspicion, and so won his absolute loyalty.

sentences.zh: 渠凶宿狡不敢發，發又輒得，士皆寒毛惕伏。

translations.literal: Veteran villains and old schemers did not dare act; when they did they were at once caught, and the soldiers trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Hardened criminals no longer dared stir; when they did they were caught at once, and the troops stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 會黃巢犯京師，帝駐梁、漢，詔從讜發部兵屬北面招討副使諸葛爽入討。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital, the emperor halted at Liang and Han; Congzan was ordered to dispatch his circuit troops to join the northern campaign deputy pacification commissioner Zhuge Shuang in advancing to punish the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao attacked the capital and the emperor withdrew to Liang and Han, Congzan was ordered to send his troops to join northern deputy pacification commissioner Zhuge Shuang against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 從讜團士五千，遣將論安從爽。

translations.literal: Congzan assembled five thousand men and sent the general Lun An to follow Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan mustered five thousand men and sent general Lun An to join Shuang.

sentences.zh: 而李克用謂太原可乘，以沙陀兵奄入其地，壁汾東，釋言討賊，須索繁仍。

translations.literal: But Li Keyong judged Taiyuan vulnerable; he led Shatuo troops in a sudden incursion, encamped east of the Fen River, and claimed he was coming to fight bandits while demanding the return of Fan Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong, however, judged Taiyuan vulnerable. He led Shatuo troops in a sudden incursion and camped east of the Fen, claiming he came to fight bandits while demanding the return of Fan Ning.

sentences.zh: 從讜以餼醪犒軍，克用隃謂曰：「我且引而南，欲與公面約。」

translations.literal: Congzan sent provisions and wine to reward the army; Keyong secretly told him: "I shall soon lead my forces south and wish to meet you face to face to make an agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan sent provisions and wine to the army. Keyong secretly told him: "I shall soon march south and wish to meet you in person.

sentences.zh: 從讜登城，開勉感概，使立功報天子厚恩，克用辭窮，再拜去。

translations.literal: Congzan mounted the wall, exhorted him earnestly and with deep feeling to achieve merit and repay the Son of Heaven's great grace; Keyong was left speechless, bowed twice, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan mounted the wall and earnestly urged him to win merit and repay the emperor's great favor. Keyong had no reply, bowed twice, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 然陰縱其下肆掠，以撼人心。

translations.literal: Yet he secretly allowed his men to loot at will to shake the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he secretly let his men plunder freely to undermine morale in the city.

sentences.zh: 從讜追安，使與將王蟾、高弁等踵擊，亦會振武契通至，與沙陀戰，沙陀大敗引還。

translations.literal: Congzan recalled An and had him, with the generals Wang Chan and Gao Bian and others, press the attack in pursuit; when Qi Tong of Zhenwu also arrived, they fought the Shatuo, who suffered a great defeat and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan recalled Lun An and sent him with Wang Chan, Gao Bian, and others in pursuit. Qi Tong of Zhenwu also arrived; they fought the Shatuo and drove them off in defeat.

sentences.zh: 即遣安等屯北百井，安擅還，從讜合諸將，命持安出，斬之鞠場。

translations.literal: He then sent An and the others to garrison Beibaijing; An returned without authorization, and Congzan assembled the generals, ordered An seized and brought out, and executed him in the review ground.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent An to garrison Beibaijing. An returned without leave. Congzan assembled the generals, had An seized, and executed him on the drill ground.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，朝廷赦沙陀，使擊賊自贖，兵不敢道太原，繇嵐、石並河而南，獨克用從數百騎過辭城下，從讜以我名馬器幣歸之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe the court pardoned the Shatuo and ordered them to attack the rebels to redeem themselves; the army dared not pass through Taiyuan but went south by way of Lan and Shi along the river; Keyong alone came with several hundred horsemen to take leave below the walls, and Congzan returned to him famous horses, vessels, and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe 2 the court pardoned the Shatuo and ordered them to fight the rebels in expiation. The army avoided Taiyuan and marched south by Lan and Shi along the river. Keyong alone came with several hundred horsemen to bid farewell below the walls, and Congzan gave him fine horses, vessels, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊平，詔克用代領河東。

translations.literal: The next year the rebels were pacified, and an edict appointed Keyong to replace Congzan in command of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after the rebels were crushed, an edict appointed Keyong to succeed Congzan as governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 克用使來曰：「方省親雁門，願公徐行。」

translations.literal: Keyong sent a messenger saying: "I am just now visiting my kin at Yanmen and ask that you go slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent word: "I am visiting my family at Yanmen and ask that you travel slowly.

sentences.zh: 從讜即日以監軍周從寓知兵馬留後，掌書記劉崇魯知觀察留後，敕克用至，按籍效之，乃行。

translations.literal: Congzan that same day appointed Army Supervisor Zhou Congyu acting military affairs intendant, Secretary Liu Chonglu acting observation intendant, and ordered that when Keyong arrived the registers be checked and handed over before he himself departed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Congzan left Army Supervisor Zhou Congyu in charge of military affairs and Secretary Liu Chonglu in charge of civil administration, instructing them to turn the registers over to Keyong when he arrived, and then departed.

sentences.zh: 黃頭軍以糧少劫其資，從讜間走絳州，方道梗不通，數月，召拜司空，復秉政，進太傅兼侍中。

translations.literal: The Yellow-Head Army, short of grain, robbed his supplies; Congzan slipped away to Jiang prefecture while the roads were blocked and impassable; after several months he was summoned as Minister of Works, again held power, and was advanced to Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow-Head troops, short of provisions, robbed his baggage. Congzan fled to Jiang while the roads were cut. Months later he was recalled as Minister of Works, returned to power, and was made Grand Tutor and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從帝至興元，以疾乞骸骨，拜太子太保，還第，卒。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Xingyuan, begged to retire on account of illness, was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, returned home, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Xingyuan, asked to retire for illness, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, went home, and died.

sentences.zh: 謚文忠。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Wenzhong, Loyal and Faithful.

sentences.zh: 從讜進止有禮法，性不矜滿，沈毅有謀。

translations.literal: Congzan's conduct was governed by ritual and law; by nature he was not arrogant or complacent, and he was deep, resolute, and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Congzan conducted himself with ritual propriety. He was neither arrogant nor complacent, and he was grave, resolute, and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 在汴時，以處誨歿於鎮，訖代，不奏樂牙中。

translations.literal: While at Bian he had lost Chuhui, who died in the commandery; until the end of his term he did not have music played in the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At Bian his brother Chuhui had died in office. Until his term ended Congzan had no music played at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 識陸扆於後生，數稱譽之，扆後位宰相。

translations.literal: He recognized Lu Yi when Yi was still young and repeatedly praised him; Yi later became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: He had recognized Lu Yi in his youth and often praised him. Yi later rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 張彥球者，拳摯善斷，累破虜有功，奏為行軍司馬，後署金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanqiu was powerful in boxing and skilled in judgment; he repeatedly defeated the enemy with merit and was memorialized as campaign secretary; later he was appointed General of the Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanqiu was a powerful fighter and a decisive judge of men. He repeatedly defeated the enemy with distinction, was made campaign secretary, and later appointed General of the Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 初，盜流中原，沙陀強悍，而卒收其用者，蓋從讜為太原重也。

translations.literal: At first bandits roamed the central plain and the Shatuo were fierce and strong; that they were finally put to use was largely because Congzan made Taiyuan secure.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits ravaged the central plain and the Shatuo were at their fiercest, it was largely because Congzan had secured Taiyuan that they were finally brought to serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 時鄭畋以宰相鎮鳳翔，移檄討賊，兩人以忠義相提衡，賊尤憚之，號「二鄭」云。

translations.literal: At the time Zheng Tian, as chief minister, garrisoned Fengxiang and issued a proclamation to attack the rebels; the two men matched each other in loyalty and righteousness, and the rebels especially feared them, calling them "the two Zhengs."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian then governed Fengxiang as chief minister and issued proclamations against the rebels. The two men matched each other in loyal resolve, and the rebels especially feared them, calling them "the two Zhengs."

sentences.zh: 鄭珣瑜

translations.literal: = Zheng Xunyu =
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xunyu

sentences.zh: 鄭珣瑜，字元伯，鄭州滎澤人。

translations.literal: Zheng Xunyu, courtesy name Yuanbo, was a man of Xingze in Zheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xunyu, styled Yuanbo, came from Xingze in Zheng prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，值天寶亂，退耕陸渾山，以養母，不幹州裏。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he encountered the Tianbao turmoil, withdrew to farm on Mount Luhun to support his mother, and did not trouble the district authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth during the Tianbao disorders, he withdrew to farm on Mount Luhun to support his mother and kept clear of local official business.

sentences.zh: 轉運使劉晏奏補寧陵、宋城尉，山南節度使張獻誠表南鄭丞，皆謝不應。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized to appoint him sheriff of Ningling and Songcheng; Shannan military governor Zhang Xiancheng recommended him as aide of Nanzheng—all he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan recommended him for posts at Ningling and Songcheng, and Shannan governor Zhang Xiancheng for aide at Nanzheng. He declined them all.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，以諷諫主文科高第，授大理評事，調陽翟丞，以拔萃為萬年尉。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he took high honors in the Remonstrance and Admonition chief civil examination, was appointed reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, was transferred to aide of Yangzhai, and by exceptional selection became sheriff of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali he placed at the top of the Remonstrance and Admonition examination, became a reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, served as aide of Yangzhai, and by exceptional selection became sheriff of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫為相，擢左補闕，出為涇原帥府判官。

translations.literal: When Cui Youfu became chief minister, Xunyu was promoted to Left Remonstrator and went out as judge on the Jingyuan commander's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Youfu became chief minister, he was promoted to Left Remonstrator and sent out as staff judge under the Jingyuan commander.

sentences.zh: 入拜侍御史、刑部員外郎，以母喪解。

translations.literal: He entered court as Attending Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, then resigned on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Attending Censor and vice director of the Ministry of Justice, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 訖喪，遷吏部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，詔擇十省郎治畿、赤，珣瑜檢校本官兼奉先令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan an edict chose bureau directors from the ten ministries to govern the capital region and Chidi; Xunyu was given acting status in his regular office and concurrently made magistrate of Fengxian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan the throne chose bureau directors from the ten ministries to govern the capital region. Xunyu was given acting rank in his regular post and concurrently made magistrate of Fengxian.

sentences.zh: 明年，進饒州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 入為諫議大夫，四遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Grand Censor and was transferred four times to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Censor and rose through four transfers to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 為河南尹。

translations.literal: He became Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He became metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 未入境，會德宗生日，尹當獻馬，吏欲前取印，白珣瑜視事，且內贄。

translations.literal: Before he had entered the circuit, it happened to be Emperor Dezong's birthday; the governor was to present horses, and clerks wished to go forward to take the seal, inform Xunyu that he should assume office, and also present a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even entered the circuit, it was Dezong's birthday. The governor was expected to present horses. Clerks wanted to take the seal, announce that Xunyu should assume office, and present a gift on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 珣瑜徐曰：「未到官而遽事獻，禮歟？」

translations.literal: Xunyu said calmly: "To rush into presenting gifts before one has even reached office—is that ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu said calmly: "To present gifts before one has even taken office—is that proper?

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 性嚴重少言，未嘗以私托人，而人亦不敢謁以私。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave and sparing of speech; he never asked favors for private ends, and others did not dare visit him on private business either.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and sparing of speech. He never asked private favors of others, and no one dared approach him on private business.

sentences.zh: 既至河南，清靜惠下，賤斂貴發以便民。

translations.literal: Once he reached Henan he governed with quiet and kindness toward subordinates, collecting little and spending much to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Henan he governed quietly and benevolently, taxing lightly and spending generously for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 方是時，韓全義將兵伐蔡，河南主饋運，珣瑜密儲之陽翟，以給官軍，百姓不知僦運勞。

translations.literal: At that time Han Quanyi led troops against Cai; Henan was responsible for supply transport. Xunyu secretly stored provisions at Yangzhai to feed the government army, and the common people did not know the labor of hired transport.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi was then campaigning against Cai and Henan supplied his transport. Xunyu secretly stockpiled grain at Yangzhai for the army, so the people never felt the burden of hired transport.

sentences.zh: 凡迎送敕使，皆在常處，吏密識其馬，進退不數步差也。

translations.literal: Whenever he welcomed or sent off imperial envoys it was always at the same place; clerks secretly knew their horses, and advance or retreat varied by no more than a few paces.
translations.idiomatic: He always received and sent off imperial envoys at the same spot. His clerks knew their horses so well that the arrangements never varied by more than a few paces.

sentences.zh: 全義與監軍別檄有所取，非詔約者，珣瑜輒掛壁不酬。

translations.literal: Quanyi and the army supervisor sent separate requisitions for items not covered by imperial orders; Xunyu would hang them on the wall and make no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi and the army supervisor sent separate demands for items not authorized by edict. Xunyu would post them on the wall and ignore them.

sentences.zh: 至軍罷，凡數百封。

translations.literal: By the time the army was disbanded there were several hundred such letters.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the campaign ended there were several hundred such letters unanswered.

sentences.zh: 有諫者曰：「軍須期會為急，公可不報？」

translations.literal: Someone admonished him: "Military supplies have urgent deadlines—can you not reply?
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him: "Military supplies have urgent deadlines. Can you not answer?

sentences.zh: 珣瑜曰：「武士統戎，多恃以取求。

translations.literal: Xunyu said: "Warriors who command armies often rely on that power to make demands.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu said: "Military commanders often use their power to make demands.

sentences.zh: 茍以為罪，尹宜坐之，終不為萬人產沴也。」

translations.literal: If this is deemed a crime, the governor ought to bear it; I will never bring harm to the livelihood of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: If that is a crime, the governor should bear it. I will never ruin the livelihood of the people.

sentences.zh: 故下無怨讟。

translations.literal: Therefore below him there was no resentment or slander.
translations.idiomatic: For that reason the people bore him no resentment.

sentences.zh: 時謂治河南比張延賞，而重厚堅正過之。

translations.literal: At the time people said his governance of Henan matched Zhang Yanshang's, yet in weight, integrity, and firm uprightness he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said his governance of Henan matched Zhang Yanshang's, but in gravity, integrity, and firm uprightness he surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 復以吏部侍郎召，進門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel and advanced to Vice Secretary of the Chancellery and Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice minister of personnel and promoted to vice secretary of the Chancellery and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李實為京兆尹，剝下務進奉，珣瑜顯詰曰：「留府緡帛入有素，余者應內度支。

translations.literal: Li Shi was Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and stripped subordinates to make court offerings; Xunyu openly questioned him: "The prefecture's retained strings of silk and cloth have fixed entries; the remainder should go to the internal revenue office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, extorted his subordinates for court offerings. Xunyu openly challenged him: "The prefecture's retained funds have fixed accounts. The remainder belongs to the internal revenue office.

sentences.zh: 今進奉乃出何色邪？」

translations.literal: From what source does today's offering come?
translations.idiomatic: What account does today's offering come from?

sentences.zh: 具以對。

translations.literal: He answered in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi answered in detail.

sentences.zh: 實方幸，依違以免。

translations.literal: Shi was then in favor and evaded by equivocation to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was then in favor and evaded the issue to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，即遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong acceded, Xunyu was at once transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong took the throne, he was immediately made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 王叔文起州吏為翰林學士、鹽鐵副使，內交奄人，攘撓政機。

translations.literal: Wang Shuwen rose from a provincial clerk to Hanlin academician and vice commissioner of salt and iron; within he allied with eunuchs and usurped the springs of government.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuwen rose from a provincial clerk to Hanlin academician and vice salt-and-iron commissioner. He allied with eunuchs within the palace and seized control of government.

sentences.zh: 韋執誼為宰相，居外奉行。

translations.literal: Wei Zhiyi was chief minister and carried out orders from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhiyi served as chief minister and carried out Shuwen's orders in public.

sentences.zh: 叔文一日至中書見執誼，直吏曰：「方宰相會食，百官無見者。」

translations.literal: One day Shuwen came to the Secretariat to see Zhiyi; the duty clerk said: "The chief ministers are at their meal; no official may be received.
translations.idiomatic: One day Shuwen came to the Secretariat to see Zhiyi. The duty clerk said: "The chief ministers are dining. No one may be received.

sentences.zh: 叔文恚，叱吏，吏走入白，執誼起，就閣與叔文語。

translations.literal: Shuwen was enraged, rebuked the clerk, and the clerk ran in to report; Zhiyi rose and went to the side chamber to speak with Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwen was furious and rebuked the clerk. The clerk ran in to report, and Zhiyi rose and went to the side chamber to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 珣瑜與杜佑、高郢輟饔以待。

translations.literal: Xunyu, with Du You and Gao Ying, stopped their meal and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu, Du You, and Gao Ying stopped eating and waited.

sentences.zh: 頃之，吏白：「二公同飯矣。」

translations.literal: Before long a clerk reported: "The two gentlemen are dining together.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a clerk reported: "The two gentlemen are dining together.

sentences.zh: 珣瑜喟曰：「吾可復居此乎！」

translations.literal: Xunyu sighed: "How can I still sit in this office!"
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu sighed: "How can I remain in this post any longer!"

sentences.zh: 命左右取馬歸，臥家不出七日，罷為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to bring his horse and return home; he lay at home and did not go out for seven days, and was removed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his horse brought and went home. He stayed indoors for seven days and was removed to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 亦會有疾，數月卒，年六十八，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He also fell ill and died several months later at sixty-eight; posthumously he was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also fell ill and died several months later at sixty-eight. Posthumously he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太常博士徐復謚文獻，兵部侍郎李巽言：「文者，經緯天地。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Xu Fu gave the posthumous name Wenxian; Vice Minister of War Li Xun said: "Wen means to weave heaven and earth together.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices erudite Xu Fu proposed the posthumous name Wenxian. Vice Minister of War Li Xun objected: "Wen means to order heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 用二謚，非《春秋》之正，請更議。」

translations.literal: To use two posthumous names is not correct according to the Spring and Autumn Annals; I ask that it be reconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: To use two posthumous names is not correct by the standards of the Spring and Autumn Annals. I ask that it be reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 復謂：「二謚，周、漢以來有之。

translations.literal: Fu replied: "Two posthumous names have existed since the Zhou and Han dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Fu argued: "Dual posthumous names have existed since Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 威烈、慎靜，周也；

translations.literal: Weilie and Jingjing are Zhou examples;
translations.idiomatic: Weilie and Jingjing are Zhou examples;

sentences.zh: 文終、文成，漢也。

translations.literal: Wenzhong and Wencheng are Han examples.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong and Wencheng are Han examples.

sentences.zh: 況珣瑜名臣，二謚不嫌。」

translations.literal: Moreover Xunyu was a famous minister; two posthumous names are not improper.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xunyu was a renowned minister. Two posthumous names are not improper for him.

sentences.zh: 巽曰：「謚一，正也，堯、舜是也。

translations.literal: Xun said: "One posthumous name is correct; Yao and Shun are the model.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said: "One posthumous name is correct. Yao and Shun are the model.

sentences.zh: 二謚，非古也，法所不載。」

translations.literal: Two posthumous names are not ancient and are not recorded in the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Two posthumous names are not ancient practice and are not authorized by law.

sentences.zh: 詔從復議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Fu's argument.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sided with Fu.

sentences.zh: 子覃。

translations.literal: His son Tan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Tan.

sentences.zh: 子 覃覃以父蔭補弘文校書郎，擢累諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Son Tan—Tan entered office by his father's privilege as collator in the Hongwen Institute and was promoted in succession to Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan entered office through his father's privilege as collator in the Hongwen Institute and rose to Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗取五中官為和糴使，覃奏罷之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong appointed five inner eunuchs as grain-purchase commissioners; Tan memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong appointed five inner eunuchs as grain-purchase commissioners. Tan memorialized to abolish the practice.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，不恤國事，數荒昵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, he did not attend to state affairs and often indulged in dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, he neglected state affairs and often indulged in dissipation.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃方強。

translations.literal: The Tibetans were then strong.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was then at the height of its power.

sentences.zh: 覃與崔郾等廷對曰：「陛下新即位，宜側身勤政，而內耽宴嬉，外盤遊畋。

translations.literal: Tan, with Cui Yan and others, answered at court: "Your Majesty has newly acceded and ought to devote yourself diligently to government, yet within you indulge in feasting and play and without you roam in hunting.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, with Cui Yan and others, addressed the throne: "Your Majesty has newly acceded and ought to devote yourself to government, yet within you indulge in feasting and play and without you roam in hunting.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃在邊，狙候中國，假令緩急，臣下乃不知陛下所在，不敗事乎？

translations.literal: Now the Tibetans are on the frontier, watching China for an opening; if an emergency arises and your ministers do not know where Your Majesty is, will affairs not fail?
translations.idiomatic: Tibet watches our frontier for an opening. If an emergency arises and your ministers do not know where you are, will affairs not fail?

sentences.zh: 夫金繒所出，固民膏血，可使倡優無功濫被賜與？

translations.literal: Gold and silk come from the people's very blood and fat—can actors and musicians without merit be lavished with gifts?
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silk come from the people's blood and sweat. Can actors and musicians without merit be lavished with gifts?

sentences.zh: 願節用之，以所餘備邊，毋令有司重取百姓，天下之幸也。」

translations.literal: We ask that expenditures be restrained, that the surplus be used to prepare the frontier, and that officials not again exact heavily from the people—this would be the good fortune of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain spending, use the surplus for the frontier, and stop officials from exacting heavily from the people. That would be the realm's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，顧宰相蕭俛曰：「是皆何人？」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and turned to chief minister Xiao Mian, saying: "Who are these men?"
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor turned to chief minister Xiao Mian and asked: "Who are these men?"

sentences.zh: 俛曰：「諫官也。」

translations.literal: Mian replied: "Remonstrating officials."
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered: "They are remonstrating officials."

sentences.zh: 帝意解，乃曰：「朕之闕，下能盡規，忠也。」

translations.literal: The emperor's mood eased and he said: "My faults, fully admonished from below—this is loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's mood eased. He said: "To admonish my faults fully—this is loyalty."

sentences.zh: 因詔覃曰：「閣中殊不款款，後有為我言者，當見卿延英。」

translations.literal: He then told Tan: "The Secretariat has been quite unreceptive; hereafter when someone speaks for me, I shall see you in the Yanying Hall."
translations.idiomatic: He then told Tan: "The Secretariat has been unreceptive. When someone speaks for me hereafter, I shall see you in the Yanying Hall."

sentences.zh: 時閣中奏久廢，至是，士相慶。

translations.literal: At the time memorials through the Secretariat had long been neglected; now scholars congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials through the Secretariat had long been neglected. Scholars now congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 王承元徙鄭滑節度使，鎮人固留不出。

translations.literal: Wang Chengyuan was transferred to military governor of Zheng-Hua, but the garrison troops firmly detained him and would not let him leave.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyuan was transferred to Zheng-Hua, but his troops refused to let him leave.

sentences.zh: 承元請以重臣勞安其軍，詔覃為宣諭使，起居舍人王璠副之。

translations.literal: Chengyuan asked that a senior minister come to reassure the army; an edict appointed Tan as pacification commissioner, with Diarist of Attendance Wang Fan as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan asked for a senior minister to reassure the army. Tan was appointed pacification commissioner with Diarist of Attendance Wang Fan as deputy.

sentences.zh: 始，鎮人慢甚，及覃傳詔，開勖大義，軍遂安，承元乃得去。

translations.literal: At first the garrison was very arrogant; when Tan proclaimed the edict and expounded great righteousness, the army was pacified and Chengyuan was able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: At first the garrison was arrogant. When Tan proclaimed the edict and expounded the principles at stake, the army was pacified and Chengyuan was able to leave.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，擢京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli he was promoted to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoli he was made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 文宗召為翰林侍講學士，進工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong summoned him as Hanlin Lecturer-in-Attendance and advanced him to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong summoned him as Hanlin lecturer-in-attendance and promoted him to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 覃於經術該深，諄篤守正，帝尤重之。

translations.literal: Tan was broadly deep in classical learning, earnest and upright in holding to principle, and the emperor especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was deeply versed in the classics, earnest and upright, and the emperor especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔、牛僧孺知政，以覃與李德裕厚，忌其親近為助力，陽遷工部尚書，罷侍講，欲推遠之。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held power; because Tan was close to Li Deyu they feared his nearness would aid Deyu, and ostensibly promoted him to Minister of Works while removing him from lecturing, intending to push him away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin and Niu Sengru held power. Because Tan was close to Li Deyu they feared he would strengthen Deyu's faction. They ostensibly promoted him to Minister of Works but removed him from lecturing to push him aside.

sentences.zh: 帝雅向學，頗思覃，復召為侍講學士。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature inclined toward learning and missed Tan; he recalled him as lecturer-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved learning and missed Tan. He recalled him as lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 德裕既相，以為御史大夫。

translations.literal: Once Deyu became chief minister, Tan was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu became chief minister, Tan was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂殷侑善言經，其為人鄭覃比也。

translations.literal: The emperor once said Yin You spoke the classics well and that as a man he was comparable to Zheng Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said Yin You expounded the classics well and was comparable to Zheng Tan in character.

sentences.zh: 宗閔猥曰：「二人誠通經，然其議論不足取。」

translations.literal: Zongmin rudely said: "The two men do indeed know the classics, yet their opinions are not worth adopting.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin said dismissively: "They know the classics, but their opinions are not worth adopting.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「覃、侑之言，它人不欲聞，惟陛下宜聞之。」

translations.literal: Deyu said: "What Tan and You say, others do not wish to hear, but Your Majesty ought to hear it."
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "What Tan and You say, others do not wish to hear—but Your Majesty ought to hear it."

sentences.zh: 俄德裕罷，宗閔復用，覃繇戶部尚書下除秘書監。

translations.literal: Soon Deyu was removed and Zongmin returned to power; Tan was demoted from Minister of Revenue to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Deyu fell and Zongmin returned to power. Tan was demoted from Minister of Revenue to Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 宗閔得罪，遷刑部尚書，進尚書右僕射，判國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Zongmin fell from favor, Tan was transferred to Minister of Justice, advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and supervised the National University.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin fell, Tan was made Minister of Justice, then Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and supervisor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 李訓誅，帝召覃視詔禁中，遂拜同中書門下平章事，封滎陽郡公。

translations.literal: After Li Xun was executed, the emperor summoned Tan to review an edict within the palace and then appointed him Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery, enfeoffing him as Duke of Xingyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xun's execution the emperor summoned Tan to review an edict in the palace and appointed him chief minister, enfeoffing him Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 不喜文辭，病進士浮誇，建廢其科，曰：「南北朝所以不治，文采勝質厚也。

translations.literal: He disliked literary ornament, deplored the jinshi degree's extravagance, and proposed abolishing the examination, saying: "The reason the Northern and Southern Dynasties were not well governed is that literary polish outweighed solid substance.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked literary ornament and deplored the extravagance of the jinshi examination. He proposed abolishing it, saying: "The Northern and Southern Dynasties failed to govern well because literary polish outweighed solid substance.

sentences.zh: 士惟用才，何必文辭。」

translations.literal: For scholars, talent in use is what matters—why must there be literary composition?
translations.idiomatic: What matters is useful talent. Why require literary composition?

sentences.zh: 又言：「文人多佻薄。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Men of letters are mostly frivolous and shallow."
translations.idiomatic: He added that literary men were mostly frivolous and shallow.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「純薄似賦性之異，奚特進士？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Purity and shallowness seem differences of innate disposition—why single out jinshi alone?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Purity and shallowness seem matters of innate disposition. Why single out jinshi candidates alone?

sentences.zh: 且設是科二百年，渠可易？」

translations.literal: Moreover this examination has stood for two hundred years—how can it be changed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this examination has stood for two hundred years. How can it be changed?

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂百司不可使一日弛惰，因指香案爐曰：「此始華好，用久則晦，不治飾，何由復新？」

translations.literal: The emperor once said the hundred offices must not be allowed a single day of laxity; pointing to the incense-stand censer he said: "At first it is bright and fine; used long it grows dim—without cleaning and polishing, how can it become new again?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said the hundred offices must never slacken for a day. Pointing to an incense censer he said: "At first it is bright and fine, but with long use it grows dim. Without care, how can it be made new again?

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「救世之敝，在先責實。

translations.literal: Tan said: "To remedy the ills of the age, the first step is to demand substance in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "To remedy the age's ills, the first step is to demand real performance.

sentences.zh: 比皆不攝職事，至慕王夷甫，以不及為靳。

translations.literal: Lately none attend to their duties; they even admire Wang Yifu and take pride in not being involved.
translations.idiomatic: Lately officials neglect their duties. Some even admire Wang Yifu and take pride in staying aloof.

sentences.zh: 此本於治平，人人無事，安逸致然。」

translations.literal: This ultimately stems from long peace: when everyone has nothing to do, ease and comfort bring it about."
translations.idiomatic: This ultimately stems from long peace. When everyone has little to do, ease and comfort produce such attitudes."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「要在謹法度而已。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The key is simply to keep to law and regulation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What matters is simply to uphold law and proper regulation."

sentences.zh: 進門下侍郎、弘文館大學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Secretary of the Chancellery and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice secretary of the chancellery and grand academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝坐延英論詩工否，覃曰：「孔子所刪，三百篇是已，其非雅正者，烏足為天子道哉？

translations.literal: The emperor sat at Yanying Hall discussing whether poetry was well crafted; Tan said: "What Confucius edited amounts to three hundred pieces—those not upright and correct, how can they suffice as a way for the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: At Yanying Hall the emperor discussed whether poetry was well made. Tan said: "Confucius edited the anthology to three hundred pieces. What is not upright and correct is hardly fit to serve as instruction for a ruler.

sentences.zh: 夫《風》、大小《雅》，皆下刺上之變，非上化下為之。

translations.literal: The Airs and the Greater and Lesser Elegantiae—all are changes in which the lower reproves the upper; they are not made by the upper transforming the lower.
translations.idiomatic: The Airs and the Greater and Lesser Elegantiae are all cases of subordinates criticizing superiors, not works in which rulers educate their people.

sentences.zh: 故王者采詩，以考風俗得失。

translations.literal: Therefore kings gather poems to examine the gains and losses of custom and mores.
translations.idiomatic: That is why kings collected poems to assess the strengths and failings of public customs.

sentences.zh: 若陳後主、隋煬帝特能詩之章解，而不知王術，故卒歸於亂。

translations.literal: If one takes Chen Houzhu and Emperor Yang of Sui, who were especially able at composing and explaining poetry, yet did not know the arts of kingship, they therefore in the end came to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu and Emperor Yang of Sui were both exceptionally skilled at poetry, yet neither knew the arts of kingship—and both ended in disorder.

sentences.zh: 章什諓諓，願陛下不取也。」

translations.literal: Composed in chapters, obsequious and flattering—I beg Your Majesty not to adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: Polished verses written to flatter—I hope Your Majesty will not prize them.

translations.literal: End of speech.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded.

sentences.zh: 帝每言：「順宗事不詳實，史臣韓愈豈當時屈人邪？

translations.literal: The emperor often said: "The affairs of Emperor Shunzong are not fully truthful—was the historian Han Yu not a man slighted in his own day?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often said: "The record of Emperor Shunzong's reign is incomplete. Was the historian Han Yu someone wronged in his own time?

sentences.zh: 昔漢司馬遷《與任安書》，辭多怨懟，故《武帝本紀》多失實。」

translations.literal: In antiquity Sima Qian of Han, in his Letter to Ren An, used many words of resentment and complaint; hence the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu contains much that is not factual.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Sima Qian's Letter to Ren An was full of resentment, and the Basic Annals of Emperor Wu accordingly fails to portray him accurately.

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「武帝中年大發兵事邊，生人耗瘁，府庫殫竭，遷所述非過言。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "In mid-life Emperor Wu greatly raised armies and fought on the borders; living people were exhausted and depleted, the treasury was drained—what Qian described was not excessive speech."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "In mid-life Emperor Wu launched major border campaigns. The people were exhausted and the treasury drained. What Qian wrote was not an exaggeration."

sentences.zh: 李石曰：「覃所陳，因武帝以諫，欲陛下終究盛德。」

translations.literal: Li Shi said: "What Tan has stated, using Emperor Wu to remonstrate, aims to have Your Majesty ultimately complete your great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi said: "Tan used Emperor Wu as a lesson in order to urge Your Majesty to finish your virtuous reign well."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Truly so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is so.

sentences.zh: 靡不有初，鮮克有終。」

translations.literal: There is hardly one without a good beginning, yet few see it through to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Few beginnings lack promise, yet few are carried through to the end."

sentences.zh: 覃曰：「陛下樂觀書，然要義不過一二，陛下所道是矣。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Your Majesty delights in reading books, yet the essential meaning amounts to no more than one or two points—what Your Majesty has just said is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Your Majesty loves reading, but the essential lesson comes down to one or two points—and what you have just said is exactly right.

sentences.zh: 宜寢饋以之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should sleep and rise with this principle."
translations.idiomatic: You should live by it day and night."

translations.literal: End of speech.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded.

sentences.zh: 覃既名儒，故以宰相領祭酒，請太學《五經》，經置博士，祿廩比王府官。

translations.literal: Since Tan was a famous Confucian, as chief minister he also served as Director of the Directorate of Education; he requested the Five Classics at the Imperial Academy, with a doctor appointed for each classic, and salary and grain rations comparable to princely household officials.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tan was a celebrated scholar, he served as chief minister while also heading the Directorate of Education. He asked that the Imperial Academy teach the Five Classics, with a doctor for each, and that their salaries and rations match those of princely household officers.

sentences.zh: 再遷太子太師。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，旱，帝多出宮人，李玨入賀曰：「漢制，八月選人；

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng there was drought; the emperor released many palace women; Li Jue entered to offer congratulations and said: "Under Han rule, in the eighth month they selected people;
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3, during a drought, the emperor released many palace women. Li Jue came to offer congratulations and said: "Under Han practice, palace women were selected in the eighth month;

sentences.zh: 晉武帝平吳，多采擇；

translations.literal: when Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu, he took many in selection;
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Wu of Jin conquered Wu, he took many for his harem;

sentences.zh: 仲尼所謂未見好德者。

translations.literal: this is what Confucius called never having seen one who loves virtue.
translations.idiomatic: as Confucius said when he observed that he had never seen anyone who truly loved virtue.

sentences.zh: 陛下以為無益，放之，盛德也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty considered it without benefit and released them—this is great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty saw no benefit in keeping them and let them go—that is great virtue.

sentences.zh: 覃又推贊曰：「晉以采擇之失，舉天下為左衽，宜陛下以為殷鑒。」

translations.literal: Tan again extended praise and said: "Jin, through the error of selection, turned all under Heaven to wear the left lapel—Your Majesty should take this as a bright mirror."
translations.idiomatic: Tan added his praise: "Jin, for its lust in taking women, brought the whole realm to submit to barbarian ways. Your Majesty should take that as a warning."

sentences.zh: 帝善其將美。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his intent to beautify.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed his effort to praise him.

sentences.zh: 以病乞去位，有詔解太子太師，許五日一入中書，商量政事。

translations.literal: On account of illness he begged to leave office; an edict relieved him of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and permitted him to enter the Secretariat once every five days to discuss government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to ask to step down. An edict removed him as grand preceptor of the heir apparent but allowed him to enter the Secretariat once every five days to advise on policy.

sentences.zh: 俄罷為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed and made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 武宗初，李德裕復用，欲援覃共政，固辭，乃授司空，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuzong, Li Deyu was again employed; wishing to draw Tan to share in government, Tan firmly declined; thereupon he was appointed Minister of Works, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wuzong's reign Li Deyu returned to power and tried to bring Tan back into government. Tan firmly declined, was made Minister of Works, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 覃清正退約，與人未嘗串狎。

translations.literal: Tan was upright, pure, retiring, and restrained; with others he never mixed in familiar intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was upright, modest, and austere. He never mingled familiarly with others.

sentences.zh: 位相國，所居第不加飾，內無妾媵。

translations.literal: Though he held the rank of chief minister, the residence he lived in was not augmented with decoration, and inside there were no concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Even as chief minister he did not embellish his house, and he kept no concubines.

sentences.zh: 女孫適崔臯，官裁九品衛佐，帝重其不昏權家。

translations.literal: His granddaughter by a daughter married Cui Gao, whose office was only a ninth-rank guard adjutant; the emperor valued that he did not marry into powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: His granddaughter married Cui Gao, who held only a ninth-rank guard post. The emperor respected that he did not marry into powerful families.

sentences.zh: 覃之侍講，每以厚風俗、黜朋比再三為天子言，故終為相。

translations.literal: In Tan's lecturing service, he repeatedly spoke to the Son of Heaven about enriching custom and mores and dismissing factional alliances; therefore he finally became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: As lecturer he repeatedly urged the emperor to strengthen public morals and curb factional cliques, and that is why he eventually rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 然疾惡多所不容，世以為太過，憚之。

translations.literal: Yet in hating evil he tolerated little, and the world thought this excessive and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was fierce in condemning wrongdoing and little tolerated, which many thought excessive—and they feared him.

sentences.zh: 始，覃以經籍刓繆，博士陋淺不能正，建言：「願與巨學鴻生共力讎刊，準漢舊事，鏤石太學，示萬世法。」

translations.literal: At the start Tan, because the classics were corrupted and erroneous and the doctors were shallow and could not correct them, submitted a proposal: "I wish to join with great scholars and eminent men of learning in concert to collate and correct them, following Han precedent, carving them in stone at the Imperial Academy to display a model for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Tan saw that the classics were corrupt and that the academy readers were too shallow to fix them. He proposed: "Let me work with leading scholars to collate and correct the texts, follow Han precedent, and carve them on stone at the Imperial Academy as a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 覃乃表周墀、崔球、張次宗、孔溫業等是正其文，刻於石。

translations.literal: Tan thereupon memorialized Zhou Chi, Cui Qiu, Zhang Cizong, Kong Wenye, and others to rectify the text and carve it on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then appointed Zhou Chi, Cui Qiu, Zhang Cizong, Kong Wenye, and others to correct the texts and cut them in stone.

sentences.zh: 子裔綽。

translations.literal: His son was Yi Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yi Chuo.

sentences.zh: 裔綽峭立有父風，以門蔭進，為李德裕所知，擢渭南尉。

translations.literal: Yi Chuo stood sharp and upright with his father's manner; by inherited privilege he entered service, was recognized by Li Deyu, and was promoted to Weinan district captain.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Chuo inherited his father's sharp integrity. He entered office by privilege, won Li Deyu's notice, and was promoted to captain of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 直弘文館，累遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He served directly in the Hongwen Hall and was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served at the Hongwen Hall and rose to remonstrance censor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，劉潼繇鄭州刺史授桂管觀察使，裔綽固爭：「潼被責未久，不宜付廉察。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzong, Liu Tong was transferred from Governor of Zheng prefecture to Observation Commissioner of Guiguan; Yi Chuo firmly objected: "Tong was censured not long ago—he should not be entrusted with provincial inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign Liu Tong was moved from governor of Zheng to Guiguan observation commissioner. Yi Chuo objected forcefully: "Tong was recently punished. He should not be given an inspection post.

sentences.zh: 帝已遣使者頒詔，追罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor had already sent a messenger to promulgate the edict but recalled and cancelled it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already sent an envoy with the appointment but recalled him and cancelled the order.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。
