translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made drafting secretary.

sentences.zh: 楊漢公為荊南節度使，坐貪沓，貶秘書監，尋拜同州刺史，裔綽與鄭公輿封還制書。

translations.literal: Yang Hangong was Military Governor of Jingnan; convicted of greed and stinginess, he was demoted to Director of the Secretariat; soon he was appointed Governor of Tong prefecture; Yi Chuo and Zheng Gongyu sealed and returned the appointment document.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hangong, military governor of Jingnan, was demoted to director of the secretariat for corruption, then almost immediately appointed governor of Tong. Yi Chuo and Zheng Gongyu sealed up the appointment and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 帝自即位，諫臣規正無不納。

translations.literal: From the time the emperor took the throne, remonstrance officials who corrected him—none of their advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne the emperor had accepted every corrective word from his remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 至是，有為漢公地者，遂終不易。

translations.literal: At this point someone pleaded Hangong's case, and in the end the appointment was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: This time someone spoke for Hangong, and the appointment stood.

sentences.zh: 會賜宴禁中，天子擊球，至門下官，謂二人曰：「近論漢公事，類朋黨者。」

translations.literal: Once, at a banquet granted within the Forbidden City, the Son of Heaven played ball; coming to the Gate officials he said to the two men: "Your recent discussion of Hangong's affair resembled factionalists.
translations.idiomatic: At a palace banquet the emperor was playing ball. When he reached the Gate officials he said to the two men: "Your recent objections over Hangong looked like partisan collusion.

sentences.zh: 裔綽曰：「同州，太宗興王地，陛下為人子孫，當慎所付。

translations.literal: Yi Chuo said: "Tong prefecture is the ground where Taizong rose to kingship; Your Majesty, as a descendant, should be careful whom you entrust.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Chuo said: "Tong is where Taizong began his rise. As his descendant, Your Majesty should choose its governor with care.

sentences.zh: 且漢公墨沒敗官，奈何以重地私之？」

translations.literal: Moreover Hangong is corrupt and failed in office—how can you privately favor him with an important post?"
translations.idiomatic: And Hangong is a corrupt failure—how can you favor him with so important a post?"

sentences.zh: 帝變色。

translations.literal: The emperor changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened.

sentences.zh: 翌日，貶商州刺史。

translations.literal: The next day he was demoted to Governor of Shang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yi Chuo was demoted to governor of Shang.

sentences.zh: 時猶衣綠，因詔賜緋魚。

translations.literal: At the time he still wore green; therefore an edict bestowed crimson and fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was still wearing green at the time, so the emperor granted him crimson robes and a fish tally.

sentences.zh: 後繇秘書監遷浙東觀察使，終太子少保。

translations.literal: Later, from Director of the Secretariat he was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Zhedong, and ended as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later moved from director of the secretariat to Zhedong observation commissioner and ended as junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 覃弟朗。

translations.literal: Tan had a younger brother, Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brother was Lang.

sentences.zh: 朗，字有融，始辟柳公綽山南幕府，入遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: Lang, courtesy name Yourong, was first recruited into Liu Gongchuo's staff in Shannan, entered the capital, and was transferred to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Lang, styled Yourong, first joined Liu Gongchuo's staff in Shannan, came to court, and was made right reminder.

sentences.zh: 開成中，擢起居郎。

translations.literal: During Kaicheng he was promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaicheng he was promoted to diarist.

sentences.zh: 文宗與宰相議政，適見朗執筆螭頭下，謂曰：「向所論事，亦記之乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong was discussing government with the chief minister; seeing Lang holding his brush beneath the dragon head, he said: "The matters just discussed—are you recording them too?
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong was conferring with his chief minister when he noticed Lang writing beneath the dragon head. He asked: "Are you recording what we just discussed?

sentences.zh: 朕將觀之。」

translations.literal: I wish to view them.
translations.idiomatic: I would like to read them.

sentences.zh: 朗曰：「臣執筆所書者，史也。

translations.literal: Lang said: "What this subject records with brush in hand is history.
translations.idiomatic: Lang said: "What I write with this brush is history.

sentences.zh: 故事，天子不觀史，昔太宗欲觀之，朱子奢曰：『史不隱善，不諱惡。

translations.literal: By precedent the Son of Heaven does not view the history; formerly Taizong wished to view it; Zhu Zishuo said: "History does not hide the good and does not conceal the bad."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent emperors did not read the draft history. When Taizong once asked to see it, Zhu Zishuo said: "History hides neither good nor evil."

sentences.zh: 自中主而下，或飾非護失，見之，則史官無以自免，且不敢直筆。』

translations.literal: From middling rulers downward, some gloss over wrongs and shield faults; if they see the record, then the historiographers have no way to exempt themselves and moreover dare not write straight.
translations.idiomatic: From mediocre rulers on down, some conceal faults. If they read the record, historians cannot protect themselves and no longer dare write plainly.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良亦稱：『史記天子言動，雖非法必書，庶幾自飭。』」

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang also said: "The historical record of the Son of Heaven's words and actions, though not lawful must be written, that perhaps he may restrain himself."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang also said: "The record must set down the emperor's words and deeds even when they are wrong, so that he may learn to restrain himself."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，謂宰相曰：「朗援故事，不畀朕見起居註，可謂善守職者。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said to the chief minister: "Lang cites precedent and does not let Us view the Daily Record—it may be said he well guards his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and told the chief minister: "Lang cites precedent and keeps me from the Daily Record. He truly guards his duty.

sentences.zh: 然人君之為，善惡必記，朕恐平日言之不葉治體，為將來羞，庶一見，得以自改。」

translations.literal: Yet a ruler's conduct, good or bad, must be recorded; We fear that on ordinary days Our words do not accord with the body of governance and will become shame in the future; We hope by one viewing to be able to reform Ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Yet everything a ruler does, good or bad, must be written down. I fear my daily words may not fit proper governance and will shame me later. One reading might help me reform."

sentences.zh: 朗遂上之。

translations.literal: Lang thereupon submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Lang then submitted the record.

sentences.zh: 累遷諫議大夫，為侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Censor and served as Lecturer-in-Attendance Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to remonstrance censor and served as lecturer-in-attendance academician.

sentences.zh: 由華州刺史入拜御史中丞、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: From Governor of Hua prefecture he entered and was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: From governor of Hua he entered court as vice censor-in-chief and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 為鄂嶽、浙西觀察使，進義武、宣武二節度。

translations.literal: He served as Observation Commissioner of Eyue and Zhexi, and advanced to the two military governorships of Yiwu and Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as observation commissioner of Eyue and Zhexi, then rose to military governor of both Yiwu and Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 歷工部尚書判度支、御史大夫，復為工部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He passed through Minister of Works with concurrent control of fiscal affairs and Censor-in-Chief, again became Minister of Works and Participating Secretary jointly with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as minister of works with control of fiscal affairs and as censor-in-chief, then again as minister of works and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 中人李敬寔排朗騶導馳去，朗以聞。

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Jingshi pushed Lang's outriders aside and galloped away; Lang reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Jingshi shouldered aside Lang's escort and galloped past. Lang reported the incident.

sentences.zh: 宣宗詰敬寔，自言供奉官不避道，帝曰：「傳我命則絕道行可也，而私出，不避宰相邪？」

translations.literal: Xuanzong questioned Jingshi; he himself said that as a palace attendant he did not yield the road; the emperor said: "If you were conveying My command, blocking the road would be acceptable—but going out privately, do you not yield to the chief minister?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong questioned Jingshi, who said palace attendants need not yield the road. The emperor said: "If you were carrying my orders, you might block the road. But on a private errand, will you not yield to a chief minister?

sentences.zh: 即斥敬寔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jingshi was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshi was immediately dismissed.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺鄭言者，故在幕府，朗以諫臣與輔相爭得失，不論則廢職，奏徙它官。

translations.literal: Right Reminder Zheng Yan had formerly been on Lang's staff; Lang, as a remonstrance official contending over right and wrong with the chief minister, submitted that if he did not speak out he would fail his office, and memorialized to transfer Yan to another post.
translations.idiomatic: Right reminder Zheng Yan had once served on Lang's staff. Lang argued that as a remonstrance official he must dispute a chief minister's errors or fail his duty, and had Yan transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾自陳，罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: After long service, on account of illness he stated his case and was dismissed as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing illness, he stepped down and was made junior preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 始，朗舉進士，有相者言：「君當貴，然不可以科第進。」

translations.literal: At the start, when Lang competed for jinshi, a physiognomist said: "You will reach eminence, yet you cannot advance through the examination degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When Lang first took the jinshi exam, a fortune-teller said: "You will rise high, but not through the examination route.

sentences.zh: 俄而有司擢朗第一，既又覆實被放，相者賀曰：「安之。」

translations.literal: Soon the authorities ranked Lang first; then after review he was released and failed; the physiognomist congratulated him and said: "Be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ranked first, then failed on review. The fortune-teller congratulated him and said: "Be patient."

sentences.zh: 已而果相。

translations.literal: Before long he indeed became chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In time he did become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 高郢

translations.literal: = Gao Ying =
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ying

sentences.zh: 高郢，字公楚，其先自渤海徙衛州，遂為衛州人。

translations.literal: Gao Ying, courtesy name Gongchu, his ancestors moved from Bohai to Weizhou and thus became men of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ying, styled Gongchu, came from a line that had moved from Bohai to Weizhou and settled there.

sentences.zh: 九歲通《春秋》，工屬文，著《語默賦》，諸儒稱之。

translations.literal: At nine he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, was skilled at literary composition, wrote the Rhapsody on Speech and Silence, and the various Confucians praised it.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he had mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, wrote skillfully, composed the Rhapsody on Speech and Silence, and won praise from leading scholars.

sentences.zh: 父伯祥為好畤尉，安祿山陷京師，將誅之，郢尚幼，解衣請代，賊義，並貸之。

translations.literal: His father Boxiang was captain of Haochi; when An Lushan took the capital he was about to execute him; Ying was still young, removed his garment and asked to substitute; the rebels found it righteous and spared them both.
translations.idiomatic: His father Boxiang was captain of Haochi. When An Lushan seized the capital and was about to execute him, the young Ying stripped off his own clothes and begged to die in his place. The rebels were moved and spared them both.

sentences.zh: 寶應初，及進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoying he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoying he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 代宗為太后營章敬寺，郢以白衣上書諫曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong built Zhangjing Temple for the Empress Dowager, Ying, as a commoner, submitted a written remonstrance saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong built Zhangjing Temple for the empress dowager, Ying, though still a commoner, submitted a written remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 陛下大孝因心，與天罔極，烝烝之思，要無以加。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's great filial piety arises from the heart, equal with Heaven without limit; the ever-growing thought—nothing can be added to it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial devotion springs from the heart and matches Heaven itself. Your longing for the empress dowager could scarcely be greater.

sentences.zh: 臣謂悉力追孝，誠為有益，妨時剿人，不得無損。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that exerting all strength to pursue filial piety is truly beneficial, but obstructing the times and cutting down people cannot be without harm.
translations.idiomatic: I believe wholehearted devotion to filial piety is worthy, yet projects that disrupt the season and burden the people cannot fail to do harm.

sentences.zh: 舍人就寺，何福之為？

translations.literal: Having a palace attendant enter the temple—what blessing is in that?
translations.idiomatic: What blessing comes from lodging a palace attendant in a temple?

sentences.zh: 昔魯莊公、丹桓公廟楹而刻其桷，《春秋》書之為非禮。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Zhuang of Lu painted Duke Huan's temple pillars and carved its rafters; the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded this as contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Duke Zhuang of Lu painted Duke Huan's temple pillars and carved its rafters. The Spring and Autumn Annals condemned this as unritual.

sentences.zh: 漢孝惠、孝景、孝宣令郡國諸侯立高祖、文、武廟，至元帝，與博士、議郎斟酌古禮，一罷之。

translations.literal: Emperors Xiaohui, Xiaojing, and Xiaoxuan of Han ordered the commanderies, kingdoms, and feudal lords to establish temples to Gaozu, Wen, and Wu; by the time of Emperor Yuan, with academicians and deliberation officers he weighed ancient ritual and abolished them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Xiaohui, Xiaojing, and Xiaoxuan ordered the regions to build temples to Gaozu, Wen, and Wu. By Yuan's reign the throne, with academicians and deliberation officers, reviewed ancient ritual and abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 夫廟猶不越禮而立，況寺非宗祏所安、神靈所宅乎？

translations.literal: If even temples are not established beyond ritual, how much more is a monastery not where ancestral tablets rest and spirits dwell?
translations.idiomatic: If even temples must not be built beyond ritual limits, how much less is a monastery a fitting seat for ancestral spirits?

sentences.zh: 殫萬人之力，邀一切之報，其為不可亦明矣。

translations.literal: Exhausting the strength of ten thousand men to seek an immediate recompense—the unacceptability of this is also clear.
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust the labor of multitudes in hope of instant reward is plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 間者昆吾孔熾，薦食生人，百姓懍懍，無日不惕。

translations.literal: Recently Kunwu burned fiercely, repeatedly devouring the living; the hundred surnames were fearful and apprehensive, without a day not vigilant.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the western tribes have grown fierce, preying on the living. The people live in daily fear.

sentences.zh: 遣將攘卻，亡尺寸功，隴外壤地，委諸豺狼。

translations.literal: Generals were sent to repel and drive them back, but not an inch of merit was gained; lands beyond Long, the frontier soil, were abandoned to wolves and jackals.
translations.idiomatic: Generals sent to drive them back won no ground. Frontier lands west of Long have been left to the wolves.

sentences.zh: 太宗難之業，傳之陛下，一夫不獲，尺土見侵，告成之時，猶恐有闕。

translations.literal: The enterprise Taizong found difficult has been transmitted to Your Majesty; if one man is not provided for, if one foot of soil is invaded—at the time of reporting completion one still fears there are lapses.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's hard-won legacy is now yours. If even one man lacks his due or one span of soil is lost, the realm is not complete—and you should still fear falling short.

sentences.zh: 況用武以來十三年，傷者不救，死者不收，繕卒補乘，於今未已。

translations.literal: Moreover since the use of arms began, thirteen years: the wounded are not rescued, the dead are not gathered, mending soldiers and filling chariots—to this day it has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover war has gone on for thirteen years. The wounded go untreated, the dead unburied, and conscription to fill the ranks still has not stopped.

sentences.zh: 夫興師十萬，日費千金，計十三年，舉百萬之眾，資糧屝屨，取足於人，勞罷宛轉，十不一在。

translations.literal: Raising an army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand gold pieces a day; reckoning thirteen years, mobilizing a multitude of a million—provisions, grain, straw sandals—all taken fully from the people; laboring and exhausted, turning and twisting, not one in ten remains.
translations.idiomatic: An army of a hundred thousand costs a thousand gold a day. Over thirteen years a million men have been mobilized, their food and gear drawn entirely from the people. Most are worn out—and fewer than one in ten remains fit for service.

sentences.zh: 父子兄弟，相視無聊，延頸嗷嗷，以役王命。

translations.literal: Fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, face one another without hope; craning their necks they cry out, compelled by the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers, sons, and brothers stare at one another in despair, throats raised in protest, yet bound to imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 縱未能出禁財，贍鰥寡，猶當稍息勞敝，以噢休之。

translations.literal: Even if unable to disburse forbidden-store wealth to nourish widows and orphans, still one ought slightly to rest labor and exhaustion and comfort them with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the throne cannot open the treasury to support widows and orphans, it should at least ease their exhaustion and give them some relief.

sentences.zh: 奈何戎虜未平，侵地未復，金革未戢，疲人未撫，太倉無終歲之儲，大農有榷酤之敝，欲以此時興力役哉？

translations.literal: How can it be—barbarian enemies not yet pacified, invaded lands not yet recovered, arms not yet stilled, the weary people not yet soothed, the Grand Granary without a full year's store, the Minister of Agriculture with the harm of monopoly wine—wishing at such a time to raise forced labor?
translations.idiomatic: How can forced labor be raised when the frontier is still unsettled, lost territory unrestored, war unended, the weary unrelieved, the Grand Granary empty, and the exchequer strained by the wine monopoly?

sentences.zh: 比八月雨不潤下，菽麥失時，黔首狼顧，憂在艱食，若遂不給，將何以救之？

translations.literal: Recently in the eighth month rain did not moisten the lower earth; beans and wheat missed their season; the black-headed people look back like wolves, their worry in scarcity of food—if supplies then fail, by what means will they be saved?
translations.idiomatic: This August the rains failed. Beans and wheat were sown out of season. The people look back in fear, dreading famine. If stores run out, how will they be saved?

sentences.zh: 無寺猶可，無人其可乎？

translations.literal: To go without a temple may still be possible—but to go without people, can that be possible?
translations.idiomatic: Doing without a temple may be bearable—but doing without people, can that be endured?

sentences.zh: 然土木之勤，功用之費，不虛府庫，將焉取之？

translations.literal: Yet the labor of earth and wood, the expense of effort and function—do they not empty the treasury in vain? From where will it be taken?
translations.idiomatic: Yet timber and earthworks demand real labor and real expense. The treasury cannot be drained without cost. Where will the money come from?

sentences.zh: 府庫既竭，則又誅求，若人不堪命，盜賊相挺而興，戎狄乘間，以為風塵，得不為陛下深憂乎？

translations.literal: When the treasury is already exhausted, then again there is relentless collection; if the people cannot bear the commands, bandits rise one after another, the Rong and Di seize the interval, taking it as wind and dust—must this not be deep worry for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: When the treasury runs dry, the levies grow harsh. If the people cannot endure, brigands will multiply and barbarians will seize the moment to bring chaos. Should this not deeply trouble Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人受命於天，以人為主，茍功濟於天，天人同和，則宗廟受福，子孫蒙慶。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the sage receives the mandate from Heaven, taking the people as master; if merely merit aids Heaven, Heaven and man equally harmonize, then the ancestral temple receives blessing and descendants receive felicity.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a sage receives Heaven's mandate to rule for the people. When human effort aligns with Heaven, the ancestral temple is blessed and descendants prosper.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「德教加於百姓，刑於四海，天子之孝也。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "When moral teaching is applied to the hundred surnames and extends over the four seas, this is the Son of Heaven's filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "When moral teaching reaches the people and extends across the realm, that is the Son of Heaven's filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「無念爾祖，聿脩厥德，」「既受帝祉，施於孫子。」

translations.literal: It also says: "Do not forget your ancestor; diligently cultivate his virtue," "Having received the emperor's blessing, extend it to your grandchildren."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "Do not forget your ancestors; diligently uphold their virtue," and "Having received Heaven's blessing, pass it to your descendants."

sentences.zh: 是知王者之孝，在於承順天地，嚴配宗考，恭慎德教，以臨兆民。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the filial piety of a king lies in inheriting and following Heaven and Earth, solemnly matching the ancestral temple and deceased father, reverently and cautiously applying moral teaching, to oversee the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the king's filial piety lies in harmonizing with Heaven and Earth, honoring the ancestral temple, and governing the people through moral example—not in lavish display.

sentences.zh: 俾四海之內，歡心助祭，延福流祚，永永無窮。

translations.literal: To make within the four seas hearts rejoice in assisting sacrifice, extending blessing and flowing grace, forever without end.
translations.idiomatic: So that within the four seas hearts unite in ritual, blessings flow, and fortune endures without end.

sentences.zh: 未聞崇樹梵宮，雕琢金玉之為孝者。

translations.literal: One has not heard of exalting and planting Buddhist monasteries, carving and polishing gold and jade, as filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: No one has ever called raising Buddhist temples and adorning them with gold and jade an act of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 夏禹卑宮室，盡力溝洫，人到於今稱之。

translations.literal: Xia Yu made his palace lowly, exerting all strength on canals and ditches; people to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu the Great kept his palace humble and poured his strength into irrigation. People praise him to this day.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝窮土木，飾塔廟，人無稱焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang exhausted earth and wood, adorned pagodas and temples; people offer him no praise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang poured everything into building and decorating temples. No one praises him for it.

sentences.zh: 陛下若節用愛人，當與夏後齊美，何必勞人動眾，踵梁武遺風乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty economizes use and cherishes the people, you should align in beauty with Lord Yu of Xia—why must you toil the people and move the multitude, following in the legacy of Emperor Wu of Liang?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty practiced frugality and cared for the people, you would rival Yu the Great. Why labor the masses and follow Liang Wudi's example?

sentences.zh: 及制作之初，支費尚淺，人貴量力，不貴必成，事貴相時，不貴必遂。

translations.literal: When construction first began, expenditure was still shallow; the people valued measuring strength, not valuing certain completion; affairs valued matching the times, not valuing certain success.
translations.idiomatic: When the project began, costs were still modest. Wise rulers weigh their strength, not blind completion, and fit their work to the times rather than insisting on finishing at any price.

sentences.zh: 陛下若回思慮，從人心，則聖德孝思，格於天地，千福萬祿，先後受之，曾是一寺較功德邪？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty turns back thought and consideration, follows the people's hearts, then sagely virtue and filial thought reach Heaven and Earth, a thousand blessings and ten thousand emoluments—the former and latter receive them; was it ever a single temple compared for merit?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty reconsidered and followed the people's will, your virtue would reach Heaven and blessings would flow in abundance. Would that not outweigh the merit of a single temple?

sentences.zh: 書奏，未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply was received.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial but received no response.

sentences.zh: 復上言：

translations.literal: Again he submitted a statement:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 王者將有為也，將有行也，必稽於眾而順於人，則自然之福，不求而至，未然之禍，不除而絕。

translations.literal: When a king is about to act and about to undertake action, he must examine the multitude and follow the people; then the natural blessing, not sought, arrives; the not-yet-happened disaster, not removed, is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler intends to act, he must consult the people and move with their will. Then blessings come unbidden and disasters are averted before they strike.

sentences.zh: 臣聞神人無功者，不為有功之功；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the divine man without merit does not act for meritorious merit;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the sage does not pursue merit for its own sake;

sentences.zh: 聖人無名者，不為有名之名。

translations.literal: the sage without name does not act for renowned name.
translations.idiomatic: nor does he seek fame for the sake of fame.

sentences.zh: 不為有功之功，故功莫大；

translations.literal: Not acting for meritorious merit, therefore merit is none greater;
translations.idiomatic: By not striving for merit, he achieves the greatest merit;

sentences.zh: 不為有名之名，故名莫厚。

translations.literal: not acting for renowned name, therefore the name is none thicker.
translations.idiomatic: by not chasing fame, he wins the highest renown.

sentences.zh: 古之明王積善以致福，不費財以求福；

translations.literal: The enlightened kings of old accumulated goodness to attain blessing, not spending wealth to seek blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Enlightened kings of old accumulated virtue to win blessing, not spent treasure to buy it;

sentences.zh: 脩德以銷禍，不勞人以攘禍。

translations.literal: cultivated virtue to dissolve disaster, not labored the people to avert disaster.
translations.idiomatic: they cultivated virtue to avert calamity, not exhausted the people to drive calamity away.

sentences.zh: 陛下之營作，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's building enterprise—your subject privately finds it puzzling.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's building projects puzzle me.

sentences.zh: 若以為功，則天覆地載，陰施陽化，未曾有為也；

translations.literal: If it is taken as merit, then Heaven covers and Earth carries, secretly bestowing and yang transforming—never has there been deliberate action;
translations.idiomatic: If you seek merit, consider how Heaven and Earth nourish all things without striving;

sentences.zh: 若以為名，則至德要道，以順天下，未曾有待也；

translations.literal: if it is taken as name, then the utmost virtue and essential Way, following the realm—never has there been waiting;
translations.idiomatic: if you seek fame, the Way of the sage needs no ostentation;

sentences.zh: 若以致福，則通於神明，光於四海，不在費財；

translations.literal: if it is taken to attain blessing, then penetrating the spirits and bright over the four seas—not in spending wealth;
translations.idiomatic: if you seek blessing, it lies in reaching the spirits and illuminating the realm, not in spending treasure;

sentences.zh: 若以攘禍，則方務厥德，罔有天災，不在勞人。

translations.literal: if it is taken to avert disaster, then squarely attending to that virtue—no heavenly disaster—not in laboring the people.
translations.idiomatic: if you seek to avert disaster, cultivate virtue; do not exhaust the people.

sentences.zh: 今興造趣急，人徒竭作，土木並起，日課萬工，不遑食息，搒笞愁痛，盈於道路。

translations.literal: Now construction is hurried urgently; corvée laborers exhaust their work; earth and wood rise together; daily assigning ten thousand workers, no leisure to eat or rest; cudgeling and flogging, sorrow and pain, fill the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Now construction rushes forward. Laborers toil without pause, thousands assigned each day with no time to eat or rest. Whippings and cries fill the roads.

sentences.zh: 以此望福，臣恐不然。

translations.literal: With this to look for blessing, your subject fears it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: To expect blessing from this, I fear, is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 陛下戢定多難，勵精思治，務行寬仁，以幸天下。

translations.literal: Your Majesty suppressed and settled many difficulties, exerted spirit and reflected on governance, earnestly practiced leniency and benevolence, to bring fortune to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ended many troubles, applied yourself to governance, and practiced leniency to bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 今固違群情，徇左右過計，臣竊為陛下惜之。

translations.literal: Now stubbornly going against the multitude's feeling, following the associates' excess plans—your subject privately regrets this for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now you defy public sentiment and follow bad counsel from those around you. I grieve this for Your Majesty's sake.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: Not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 以茂才異行高第，累擢咸陽尉。

translations.literal: Through high placement as exceptional talent and extraordinary conduct, repeatedly promoted to captain of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: On high marks for exceptional talent and conduct, he rose steadily to captain of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀取為朔方掌書記。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi took him as chief secretary of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi appointed him chief secretary in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 子儀怒判官張曇，奏抵死，郢引捄甚力，忤子儀意，下徙猗氏丞。

translations.literal: Ziyi was angry at judicial assistant Zhang Tan, memorialized for death penalty; Ying argued rescue with great force, going against Ziyi's intent, demoted and transferred to aide of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi, furious at judicial assistant Zhang Tan, petitioned for his execution, Ying argued strenuously for mercy. Offending Ziyi, he was demoted to aide of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 李懷光引佐邠寧府。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang brought him to assist the Binning headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai'guang took him on as an aide at the Binning headquarters.

sentences.zh: 懷光將還河中，郢勸不如西迎乘輿，懷光反方銳，不聽。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was about to return to Hezhong; Ying urged that it would be better to go west and welcome the imperial carriage; Huai'guang's rebellion was just sharp; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang prepared to return to Hezhong, Ying urged him instead to march west and receive the emperor. Huai'guang, flush with rebellion, refused.

sentences.zh: 既又欲悉兵鼓而西。

translations.literal: Then again he wished to gather all troops, beat drums, and go west.
translations.idiomatic: He then planned to march west with his full army.

sentences.zh: 時渾瑊提孤軍抗賊，群將未集，郢恐為懷光所乘，與李庸阝固止之。

translations.literal: At the time Hun Jian led an isolated army resisting rebels; the group of generals had not yet assembled; Ying feared Huai'guang would take advantage; with Li Yong he firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian then held a lone force against the rebels while other generals had not yet gathered. Ying feared Huai'guang would exploit the moment and, with Li Yong, firmly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 會懷光子隹候郢，郢因脅說曰：「君視天寶以來稱兵者，今尚誰在？

translations.literal: It happened that Huai'guang's son Cui waited on Ying; Ying thereupon coerced and persuaded, saying: "Sir, look at those who raised armies since the Tianbao era—who still survives today?
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'guang's son Cui came to visit, Ying pressed him: "Look at every rebel since the Tianbao era. Who among them still lives?

sentences.zh: 且國家固有天命，人力不豫焉。

translations.literal: Moreover the state inherently has Heaven's mandate; human power does not pre-order it.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has Heaven's mandate. No man can arrange it by force.

sentences.zh: 今若恃眾而動，自絕於天。

translations.literal: Now if one relies on the multitude to move, one cuts oneself off from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: To rely on numbers and rebel is to cut yourself off from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 十室之小，必得忠信，安知三軍不有奔潰而助順者乎？」

translations.literal: In a small place of ten houses one must obtain loyalty and trust—how know that among the three armies there are none who flee, collapse, and aid the obedient side?
translations.idiomatic: Even in a hamlet of ten households there are loyal men. How do you know your army will not break and join the loyal side?

sentences.zh: 隹大懼，流汗不能語。

translations.literal: Cui was greatly fearful, sweat flowing, unable to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Cui was terrified, sweating and speechless.

sentences.zh: 郢因與其將呂鳴嶽、張延英謀間道歸國，事泄，懷光先斬二將，然後引郢詰誚，郢抗詞無所愧隱，觀者為泣下。

translations.literal: Ying thereupon with his generals Lu Mingyue and Zhang Yanying plotted a secret route to return to the state; the affair leaked; Huai'guang first executed the two generals, then brought Ying to question and reproach; Ying spoke boldly without shame or concealment; observers wept.
translations.idiomatic: Ying then plotted with generals Lu Mingyue and Zhang Yanying to escape by a hidden route back to the loyal side. When the plot leaked, Huai'guang executed the two generals first, then summoned Ying to interrogate him. Ying answered boldly without shame, and onlookers wept.

sentences.zh: 懷光慚，赦之。

translations.literal: Huai'guang was ashamed and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Huai'guang spared him.

sentences.zh: 孔巢父遇害，郢撫屍而哭。

translations.literal: When Kong Chaofu was killed, Ying stroked the corpse and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Kong Chaofu was murdered, Ying mourned over his body.

sentences.zh: 懷光已誅，李晟表其忠，馬燧奏管書記。

translations.literal: After Huai'guang was already executed, Li Sheng memorialized his loyalty; Ma Sui memorialized to appoint him secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai'guang's death, Li Sheng praised his loyalty and Ma Sui recommended him as secretary.

sentences.zh: 召拜主客員外郎，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed vice director of the Bureau of Receptions for Foreign Envoys; transferred to draft secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice director of the Bureau of Receptions for Foreign Envoys and promoted to secretariat draft secretary.

sentences.zh: 久之，進禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After long time, promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時四方士務朋比，更相譽薦，以動有司，徇名亡實。

translations.literal: At the time scholars from the four directions devoted themselves to faction and association, mutually praising and recommending one another, to move the responsible offices, seeking name and losing substance.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere formed cliques, recommending one another to sway the examiners, chasing reputation while neglecting real merit.

sentences.zh: 郢疾之，乃謝絕請謁，顓行藝。

translations.literal: Ying was vexed by this; thereupon declined visits and requests, exclusively applying accomplishment in art.
translations.idiomatic: Ying abhorred this, refused solicitation, and judged candidates solely on merit.

sentences.zh: 司貢部凡三歲，甄幽獨，抑浮華，流競之俗為衰。

translations.literal: Directing the tribute department for altogether three years, he distinguished the obscure and solitary, suppressed the showy and florid; the custom of clamorous competition declined.
translations.idiomatic: For three years as chief examiner he favored the obscure over the flashy, and the culture of competitive showmanship faded.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，擢中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan, promoted to vice grand secretary and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan he became vice grand secretary and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，病不能事，王叔文黨根據朝廷，帝始詔皇太子監國，而郢以刑部尚書罷。

translations.literal: When Shunzong ascended, ill and unable to govern, Wang Shuwen's faction rooted itself in the court; the emperor first decreed the crown prince to supervise the state; but Ying was dismissed as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended, too ill to rule, Wang Shuwen's faction seized control. The emperor named the crown prince regent, but Ying was dismissed from his post as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 明年，為華州刺史，政尚仁靜。

translations.literal: The next year, made prefect of Hua; governance honored benevolence and quietness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became prefect of Hua, governing with quiet benevolence.

sentences.zh: 初，駱元光自華引軍戍良原。

translations.literal: At the start, Luo Yuanguang from Hua led troops to garrison Liangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Luo Yuanguang had led troops from Hua to garrison Liangyuan.

sentences.zh: 元光卒，軍入神策，而州仍歲餉其糧，民困輸入，累刺史憚不敢白，郢奏罷之。

translations.literal: Yuanguang died; the army entered the Shence Army; yet the prefecture yearly supplied their grain; the people were distressed by delivery; successive prefects feared and dared not report; Ying memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanguang died his troops joined the Shence Army, yet Hua still had to supply their grain each year. The people buckled under the burden. Prefect after prefect had feared to protest, but Ying memorialized to end the levy.

sentences.zh: 復召為太常卿，除御史大夫。

translations.literal: Again summoned as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of imperial sacrifices and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 數月，改兵部尚書，固乞骸骨，以尚書右僕射致仕。

translations.literal: Several months later, changed to minister of war; firmly begging to retire on old bones; retired as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he became minister of war, then firmly requested retirement and left office as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈太子太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died, age seventy-two; posthumously given Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two, posthumously made grand preceptor of the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 郢恭慎不與人交。

translations.literal: Ying was reverent and cautious, not associating with people.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was reserved and cautious, keeping few acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 常掌制誥，家無留稿，或勸盍如前人傳制集者，答曰：「王言不可藏私家。」

translations.literal: He often managed imperial edicts; at home there were no retained drafts; some urged why not like former men who transmitted collected edicts; he answered: "The king's words cannot be stored in a private home.
translations.idiomatic: He often drafted imperial edicts and kept no copies at home. When urged to publish a collection like earlier draftsmen, he replied: "Imperial words must not be hoarded in a private house.

sentences.zh: 生平不治產，有勸營之者，答曰：「祿稟雖薄，在我則有餘，田莊何所取乎？」

translations.literal: Through life he did not manage property; there were those who urged him to undertake it; he answered: "Salary and grain, though thin—in me there is surplus; from fields and estates what is taken?
translations.idiomatic: He never sought to build an estate. When urged to do so, he said: "My salary, though modest, is enough for me. What need have I of farmland?

sentences.zh: 郢之相也，與鄭珣瑜同拜。

translations.literal: When Ying became chief minister, he was appointed together with Zheng Xunyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying became chief minister on the same day as Zheng Xunyu.

sentences.zh: 既叔文用事，珣瑜憂甚，爭不能得，乃稱疾不出，郢未有所建白，俄與珣瑜免，故議者賢珣瑜而咎郢。

translations.literal: Once Shuwen held power, Xunyu was deeply worried; contending but unable to prevail, then claimed illness and did not go out; Ying had no proposals established; soon with Xunyu was dismissed; therefore discussers esteemed Xunyu and blamed Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuwen took power, Xunyu was deeply alarmed. Unable to prevail in debate, he feigned illness and stayed home. Ying made no protest. Both were soon dismissed, and critics praised Xunyu while blaming Ying.

sentences.zh: 子定。

translations.literal: His son Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Ding.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：王叔文雖內連甘尹，外倚奸回，以攘天權。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wang Shuwen, though internally linking with his inner faction and palace agents, externally relying on treacherous wicked men, to usurp Heaven's power.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Wang Shuwen rallied his inner faction and palace agents within and wicked allies without, all to seize imperial power.

sentences.zh: 然是時太子已長，朝無嫌罅，若珣瑜、郢與杜佑等毅然引東宮監國，執退叔文輩，其力不難。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the crown prince was already grown, the court without rifts of suspicion; if Xunyu, Ying, and Du You and others resolutely led the Eastern Palace to supervise the state, seized and removed Shuwen's group—their strength would not have been hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown prince was already grown and the court united. Had Xunyu, Ying, and Du You firmly installed the heir as regent and removed Shuwen's faction, they could easily have done so.

sentences.zh: 顧循嘿茍安，所謂焉用彼相者矣。

translations.literal: Yet they followed silence and sought ease—what is called, of what use is such a chief minister?
translations.idiomatic: Instead they kept silent and sought safety—what use were they as chief ministers?

sentences.zh: 珣瑜一忿臥第，與郢、佑固位，二者亦不足相輕重雲。

translations.literal: Xunyu in one fit of anger lay abed; with Ying and You holding their posts—the two matters also do not suffice to weigh light and heavy against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Xunyu's angry withdrawal to his bed and Ying and You's clinging to office are scarcely matters to weigh against each other.

sentences.zh: 定，辯惠，七歲讀《尚書》，至《湯誓》，跪問郢曰：「奈何以臣伐君？」

translations.literal: Ding was eloquent and clever; at seven he read the Book of Documents; reaching the Oath of Tang, he knelt and asked Ying: "How can a subject attack his lord?
translations.idiomatic: Ding was clever and quick-witted. At seven he was reading the Book of Documents. When he reached the Oath of Tang, he knelt and asked Ying: "How can a subject attack his ruler?

sentences.zh: 郢曰：「應天順人，何雲伐邪？」

translations.literal: Ying said: "To respond to Heaven and follow the people—why speak of attacking?
translations.idiomatic: Ying said: "To answer Heaven and follow the people—why call it attack?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「用命賞於祖，不用命戮於社，是順人乎？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Those who obey the command are rewarded at the ancestral altar; those who disobey are slain at the altar of soil— is this following the people?
translations.idiomatic: Ding replied: "Those who obey are rewarded at the ancestral altar; those who disobey are executed at the altar of soil—is that following the people?

sentences.zh: 郢異之。

translations.literal: Ying found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was astonished.

sentences.zh: 小字董二，世重其早惠，以字顯。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Dong'er; the age prized his early brilliance, and he was known by that name.
translations.idiomatic: His childhood name was Dong'er. His precocity was widely admired, and he was known by that name.

sentences.zh: 長通王氏《易》，為圖合八出，上圓下方，合則重，轉則演，七轉而六十四卦，六甲、八節備焉。

translations.literal: Growing up he mastered the Wang clan's Changes of the I Ching, making diagrams combining eight outward, round above and square below; combined they double, turned they unfold; seven turns yielding sixty-four hexagrams, with the six jia and eight seasonal nodes complete therein.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered the Wang school of the Changes of the I Ching and devised diagrams with eight outward projections, round above and square below. Combined they stack; turned they unfold. Seven turns yield sixty-four hexagrams, complete with the six jia and eight seasonal nodes.

sentences.zh: 仕至京兆府參軍。

translations.literal: He served to military aide of the metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to military aide of the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄭絪

translations.literal: = Zheng Yin =
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin

sentences.zh: 鄭絪，字文明，餘慶從父行也。

translations.literal: Zheng Yin, courtesy name Wenming, was of Yuqing's father's younger branch.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yin, styled Wenming, came from the younger branch of Yuqing's father's line.

sentences.zh: 幼有奇誌，善屬文，所交皆天下有名士。

translations.literal: In youth he had extraordinary resolve, skilled at literary composition; those he associated with were all famous men under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he had unusual ambition, wrote skillfully, and kept company with celebrated men throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 擢進士、宏辭高第。

translations.literal: Selected as jinshi and top in the Hongci examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and ranked at the top in the Hongci competition.

sentences.zh: 張延賞帥劍南，奏署掌書記。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang commanded Jiannan, memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanshang was military governor of Jiannan, he had Yin appointed chief secretary on his staff.

sentences.zh: 入為起居郎、翰林學士，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Entered as attendant of the palace secretariat and Hanlin academician; repeatedly promoted to draft secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as a palace attendant and Hanlin academician, then rose to secretariat draft secretary.

sentences.zh: 德宗自興元還，置六軍統軍視六尚書，以處功臣，除制用白麻付外。

translations.literal: Dezong, returning from Xingyuan, established six army commanders-in-chief equal to the six chief ministers, to place meritorious officials; appointment edicts used white hemp delivered outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong returned from Xingyuan, he created six army commanders-in-chief equal in rank to the six chief ministers to honor meritorious generals. Their appointments were drafted on white hemp and sent out directly.

sentences.zh: 又廢宣武軍，益左右神策，以監軍為中尉。

translations.literal: Also abolished the Xuanwu Army, augmenting the Left and Right Shence Armies, making the army supervisors commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished the Xuanwu Army, expanded the Left and Right Shence Armies, and made army supervisors their commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 竇文場恃功，陰諷宰相進擬如統軍比。

translations.literal: Dou Wenchang relied on merit and covertly urged the chief ministers to nominate candidates like the army commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wenchang, trading on his merit, quietly pressed the chief ministers to nominate eunuch candidates on the same terms as the army commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 絪當作制，奏言：「天子封建，或用宰相，以白麻署制，付中書、門下。

translations.literal: Yin was to draft the edict and submitted saying: "The Son of Heaven enfeoffs and establishes—sometimes using chief ministers; with white hemp he signs the edict and delivers it to the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was assigned to draft the edict and memorialized: "When the Son of Heaven enfeoffs and appoints, he sometimes uses chief ministers, who sign edicts on white hemp for the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 今以命中尉，不識陛下特以寵文場邪？

translations.literal: Now to command the commander-in-chief—does Your Majesty not recognize that this is specially to favor Wenchang?
translations.idiomatic: Now the order goes to a commander-in-chief. Does Your Majesty mean this only as a special favor to Wenchang?

sentences.zh: 遂著為令也？」

translations.literal: Or is it established as a permanent rule?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it meant to become permanent policy?

sentences.zh: 帝悟，謂文場曰：「武德、貞觀時，中人止內侍，諸衛將軍同正賜緋者無幾。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and said to Wenchang: "In the Wude and Zhenguan eras, palace attendants served only within; of the various guard generators given concurrent regular rank and bestowed crimson, there were few.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point and told Wenchang: "In the Wude and Zhenguan eras, eunuchs served only within the palace. Few guard generals were given concurrent regular rank and crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 自魚朝恩以來，無復舊制。

translations.literal: Since Yu Chao'en there has been no return to the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yu Chao'en, the old system has never been restored.

sentences.zh: 朕今用爾不謂無私，若麻制宣告，天下謂爾脅我為之。」

translations.literal: I now employ you not meaning there is no private favor—but if a hemp edict is proclaimed, the realm will say you coerced me into it.
translations.idiomatic: I appoint you now without denying personal favor—but if this edict is proclaimed on white hemp, the realm will say you forced my hand.

sentences.zh: 文場叩頭謝。

translations.literal: Wenchang knocked his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 更命中書作詔，並罷統軍用麻矣。

translations.literal: Again he ordered the Secretariat to draft the decree; also abolished using hemp for the army commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had the Secretariat draft the decree and abolished the use of white hemp for army commanders-in-chief as well.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝見絪曰：「宰相不能拒中人，得卿言乃悟。」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor saw Yin and said: "The chief ministers could not refuse the palace attendants; only on hearing your words did I understand.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor saw Yin and said: "The chief ministers could not refuse the eunuchs. Only your words made me see the point.

translations.literal: End of speech.
translations.idiomatic: (End of the emperor's remark.)

sentences.zh: 順宗病，不得語，王叔文與牛美人用事，權震中外，憚廣陵王雄睿，欲危之。

translations.literal: Shunzong was ill and could not speak; Wang Shuwen and the favored consort Niu held power; authority shook within and without; fearing the Prince of Guangling's keen intelligence, they wished to endanger him.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong was ill and unable to speak. Wang Shuwen and the favored consort Niu held power, their authority shaking court and country. Fearing the Prince of Guangling's sharp mind, they sought to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 帝召絪草立太子詔，絪不請輒書曰：「立嫡以長。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yin to draft the decree establishing the crown prince; Yin without requesting permission wrote: "Establish the legitimate heir by seniority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yin to draft the decree establishing the crown prince. Without asking further, Yin wrote: "Establish the legitimate heir by seniority.

sentences.zh: 跪白之，帝頷乃定。

translations.literal: Kneeling, he reported it; the emperor nodded, and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling, he reported it. The emperor nodded, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，遷門下侍郎。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, Yin was appointed vice director of the secretariat and concurrent chief minister, then transferred to vice director of the chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne, Yin was made vice grand secretary and chief minister, then promoted to vice chancellor.

sentences.zh: 始，盧從史陰與王承宗連和，有詔歸潞，從史辭潞乏糧，請留軍山東。

translations.literal: Earlier Lu Congshi had secretly allied with Wang Chengzong. An edict ordered him to return to Lu, but Congshi pleaded that Lu lacked grain and requested to keep his army in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi had secretly allied with Wang Chengzong. When ordered back to Lu, he pleaded lack of grain and asked to keep his army in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫密譖絪漏言於從史，帝怒，坐浴堂殿，召學士李絳語其故，且曰：「若何而處？」

translations.literal: Li Jifu secretly slandered Yin, claiming he had leaked words to Congshi. The emperor was angry. Sitting in the Bath Hall, he summoned Academician Li Jiang, told him the reason, and said: "How should this be handled?
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu secretly accused Yin of leaking secrets to Congshi. The emperor, angry, sat in the Bath Hall and summoned Li Jiang. He explained the charge and asked: "What should be done?

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「誠如是，罪當族。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "If this is truly so, the crime deserves execution of the entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said: "If that is true, the crime deserves execution of his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 然誰以聞陛下者？」

translations.literal: But who reported this to Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: But who told Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「吉甫為我言。」

translations.literal: He said: "Jifu told me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Jifu told me."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「絪任宰相，識名節，不當如犬彘梟獍與奸臣外通。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Yin serves as chief minister and understands fame and integrity. He would not be like dogs, pigs, or unfilial beasts colluding with wicked ministers abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said: "Yin is chief minister and knows honor. He would not collude with traitors like some beast.

sentences.zh: 恐吉甫勢軋內忌，造為醜辭以怒陛下。」

translations.literal: I fear Jifu, pressed by rivalry, harbors inner resentment and has fabricated ugly words to anger Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: I fear Jifu, jealous of a rival, has invented slander to anger Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝良久曰：「幾誤我！」

translations.literal: After a long silence the emperor said: "I nearly made a mistake!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor said: "I nearly made a terrible mistake!"

sentences.zh: 先是，杜黃裳方為帝夷削節度，強王室，建議裁可，不關決於絪，絪常默默。

translations.literal: Earlier Du Huangchang was then helping the emperor cut back the military commissioners and strengthen the royal house. His proposals were approved without needing Yin's consent, and Yin usually remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang was then helping the emperor weaken the military commissioners and strengthen the throne. His proposals went through without Yin, who usually said nothing.

sentences.zh: 居位四年，罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: After four years in office he was dismissed and made mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was dismissed and made mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 久乃檢校禮部尚書，出為嶺南節度使，後累遷河中節度。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made acting minister of rites and sent out as military governor of Lingnan; later he was repeatedly transferred to military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was made acting minister of rites and sent out as military governor of Lingnan, then rose to military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 入為御史大夫，檢校尚書左僕射，兼太子少保。

translations.literal: He entered court as censor-in-chief, acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and concurrent junior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as censor-in-chief, acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文宗太和中，年老乞骸骨，以太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Wenzong, old in years he begged to retire on account of age and was granted retirement as grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenzong's Taihe era he begged to retire on account of age and was granted retirement as grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，贈司空，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-eight. He was posthumously granted minister of works and given the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight, posthumously made minister of works with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 絪本以儒術進，守道寡欲，所居不為烜赫事，以篤實稱。

translations.literal: Yin had originally entered through Confucian learning. He upheld the Way and had few desires. In his conduct he did nothing ostentatious and was known for solid integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had risen through Confucian learning. He upheld the Way, wanted little, lived plainly, and was known for solid integrity.

sentences.zh: 善名理學，世以耆德推之。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the study of names and principles, and the world honored him as an elder of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in philosophical inquiry, and the world honored him as an elder of virtue.

sentences.zh: 孫顥，舉進士，以起居郎尚萬壽公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His grandson Hao passed the jinshi examination. As director of diaries he married the Princess of Wanshou and was appointed commandant of the imperial son-in-law's escort.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Hao passed the jinshi exam, married the Princess of Wanshou as director of diaries, and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law's escort.

sentences.zh: 有器識。

translations.literal: He had talent and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He had talent and discernment.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，恩寵無比。

translations.literal: In the time of Xuanzong his favor was without equal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanzong his favor was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 終檢校禮部尚書、河南尹。

translations.literal: He ended as acting minister of rites and intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as acting minister of rites and intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 權德輿

translations.literal: = Quan Deyu =
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu

sentences.zh: 權德輿，字載之。

translations.literal: Quan Deyu, courtesy name Zaizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Deyu, styled Zaizhi.

sentences.zh: 父臯，見《卓行傳》。

translations.literal: His father Gao is treated in the Biographies of Outstanding Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao is treated in the Biographies of Outstanding Conduct.

sentences.zh: 德輿七歲居父喪，哭踴如成人。

translations.literal: At seven Deyu observed mourning for his father and wept and stamped his feet like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At seven Deyu mourned his father and wept and stamped his feet like an adult.

sentences.zh: 未冠，以文章稱諸儒間。

translations.literal: Before reaching cap age he was praised among the Confucians for his literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he was praised among scholars for his writing.

sentences.zh: 韓洄黜陟河南，辟置幕府。

translations.literal: When Han Hui conducted assessments in Henan, he recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Hui conducted assessments in Henan, he recruited Deyu to his staff.

sentences.zh: 復從江西觀察使李兼府為判官。

translations.literal: He later followed Observation Commissioner Li Jian of Jiangxi as judicial assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Li Jian, observation commissioner of Jiangxi, as judicial assistant.

sentences.zh: 杜佑、裴胄交辟之。

translations.literal: Du You and Pei Zhou both repeatedly recruited him.
translations.idiomatic: Du You and Pei Zhou both recruited him.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞其材，召為太常博士，改左補闕。

translations.literal: Dezong heard of his talent and summoned him as academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then changed him to left remonstrance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong heard of his talent, summoned him as an academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then made him left remonstrance censor.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，關東、淮南、浙西州縣大水，壞廬舍，漂殺人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan, great floods in the commanderies and districts of Guandong, Huainan, and Zhexi destroyed dwellings and drowned people.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 8, great floods in Guandong, Huainan, and Zhexi destroyed homes and drowned people.

sentences.zh: 德輿建言：「江、淮田一善熟，則旁資數道，故天下大計，仰於東南。

translations.literal: Deyu submitted a proposal: "When the fields of the Yangzi and Huai have one good harvest, they supply several circuits. Thus the great plan of the realm depends on the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted: "One good harvest in the Yangzi and Huai regions supplies several circuits. The realm's great plan depends on the southeast.

sentences.zh: 今霪雨二時，農田不開，庸亡日眾。

translations.literal: Now continuous rain for two seasons has left farmland unopened, and the wandering destitute grow daily.
translations.idiomatic: Now endless rain for two seasons has left fields unplanted, and the destitute grow daily.

sentences.zh: 宜擇群臣明識通方者，持節勞徠，問人所疾苦，蠲其租入，與連帥守長講求所宜。

translations.literal: It is fitting to select from the ministers those of clear understanding and broad competence, send them with imperial credentials to comfort and encourage the people, inquire into their suffering, remit their rents and levies, and with circuit commanders and local magistrates discuss what is suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Choose clear-sighted ministers, send them with imperial credentials to comfort the people, learn their hardships, remit rents, and work with local officials on relief.

sentences.zh: 賦取於人，不若藏於人之固也。」

translations.literal: To take taxes from the people is not as solid as keeping wealth stored among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes taken from the people are less secure than wealth kept among the people.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣奚陟等四人循行慰撫。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon sent Xi Zhi and three others to tour and comfort the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xi Zhi and three others to tour the region and offer relief.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡以巧幸進，判度支，德輿上疏斥言：「延齡以常賦正額用度未盡者為羨利，以誇己功；

translations.literal: Pei Yanling advanced through deft favor and served as director of the treasury. Deyu submitted a memorial denouncing him: "Yanling treats what remains of regular tax quotas after expenses as surplus profit to boast of his achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling rose through flattery and controlled the treasury. Deyu memorialized against him: "Yanling treats unused regular tax quotas as surplus to boast of his achievement;

sentences.zh: 用官錢售常平雜物，還取其直，號別貯羨錢，因以罔上；

translations.literal: he uses official funds to sell Ever-Normal granary goods, then takes back their price, calling it separately stored surplus money, and thereby deceives his superiors;
translations.idiomatic: he uses official funds to sell Ever-Normal granary goods, takes back the price, calls it surplus stored separately, and deceives his superiors;

sentences.zh: 邊軍乏，不稟糧，召禍疆場，其事不細。

translations.literal: frontier armies lack supplies and receive no grain rations, inviting disaster on the borders—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: frontier armies lack grain rations, inviting disaster on the borders. This is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 陛下疑為流言，胡不以新利召延齡，質核本末，擇中朝臣按覆邊資。

translations.literal: Your Majesty suspects this is rumor—why not summon Yanling on the pretext of new profits, verify the facts from root to branch, and choose a court minister to investigate frontier funds?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty suspects rumor, summon Yanling on the pretext of new profits, verify the facts, and send a court minister to audit frontier funds.

sentences.zh: 如言者不謬，則邦國之務，不宜委非其人。」

translations.literal: If what is said is not false, then affairs of state must not be entrusted to such a man.
translations.idiomatic: If the charges are true, state affairs must not be left to such a man.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but ignored.

sentences.zh: 遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to diaries attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made diaries attendant.

sentences.zh: 歲中，兼知制誥，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: Within the year he additionally handled imperial edicts and was advanced to secretariat drafting attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he also handled imperial edicts and was promoted to secretariat drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 當是時，帝親攬庶政，重除拜，凡命諸朝，皆手制中下。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor personally handled ordinary governance, valued appointments and dismissals, and for every order to the court he personally drafted and issued it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor personally handled governance, valued appointments, and personally drafted every court order.

sentences.zh: 始，德輿知制誥，而徐岱給事中，高郢為舍人。

translations.literal: At first Deyu handled edicts, Xu Dai was drafting secretary, and Gao Ying was attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At first Deyu handled edicts while Xu Dai was drafting secretary and Gao Ying was attendant.

sentences.zh: 居數歲，岱卒，郢知禮部，德輿獨直兩省，數旬一還舍，乃上書言：「左右掖垣，承天子誥命，奉行詳覆，各有攸司。

translations.literal: After several years Dai died. Ying oversaw the Ministry of Rites. Deyu alone staffed both secretariats, returning home only once every several tens of days. He submitted a memorial saying: "The left and right palace gates receive the Son of Heaven's commands, carry them out, examine and review them—each has its proper office.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Dai died. Ying oversaw the Ministry of Rites. Deyu alone staffed both secretariats, returning home only every few weeks. He memorialized: "The left and right palace gates receive the emperor's commands, carry them out, and review them—each has its proper office.

sentences.zh: 舊制，分曹十員，以相防檢。

translations.literal: Under the old system there were ten officers divided by bureau to check one another.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system ten officers in separate bureaus checked one another.

sentences.zh: 大抵事有所壅，則吏得為非。

translations.literal: Generally when business is blocked, clerks can do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When business is blocked, clerks can do wrong.

sentences.zh: 四方聞者，或以朝廷為乏士，要重之司，不宜久廢。」

translations.literal: Those who hear of this throughout the four directions may think the court lacks men. Such important offices should not be left vacant long.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the realm may think the court lacks men. Such important offices should not stay vacant long.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非不知卿之勞，但擇如卿者未得其人耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is not that I do not know your labors—but I have not yet found men like you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I know your burden, but I have not yet found men like you."

sentences.zh: 久之，知禮部貢舉，真拜侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long time he oversaw the Ministry of Rites examinations and was formally appointed vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he oversaw the Ministry of Rites examinations and was formally appointed vice minister.

sentences.zh: 凡三歲，甄品詳諦，所得士相繼為公卿、宰相。

translations.literal: For three years he evaluated candidates with meticulous care. Those he selected successively became high ministers and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: For three years he evaluated candidates with meticulous care. Those he chose rose to high office and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 取明經初不限員。

translations.literal: At first there was no quota limit for those passing the classics examination.
translations.idiomatic: At first there was no quota for classics examination passers.

sentences.zh: 十九年，大旱，德輿因是上陳闕政曰：「陛下齋心減膳，閔惻元元，告於宗廟，禱諸天地，一物可祈，必致其禮，一士有請，必聽其言，憂人之心可謂至已。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year there was great drought. Deyu thereupon submitted faults in governance: "Your Majesty has purified your heart and reduced your meals, grieved for the common people, reported to the ancestral temple, and prayed to Heaven and Earth. For every thing that can be prayed for you have performed every rite; for every scholar who has a request you have listened. Your concern for the people can be called utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year there was great drought. Deyu submitted faults in governance: "Your Majesty has purified your heart, reduced your meals, grieved for the people, prayed at the ancestral temple and to Heaven and Earth. You have performed every rite and heard every plea. Your concern for the people could not be greater.

sentences.zh: 臣聞銷天災者脩政術，感人心者流惠澤，和氣洽，則祥應至矣。

translations.literal: I have heard that to dissolve heavenly disaster one must improve governance; to move people's hearts one must spread benevolent grace. When harmonious qi pervades, auspicious responses arrive.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that heavenly disaster is dispelled by good governance, and hearts are moved by grace. When harmony prevails, auspicious signs follow.

sentences.zh: 畿甸之內，大率赤地而無所望，轉徙之人，斃踣道路，慮種麥時，種不得下。

translations.literal: Within the capital region most land is bare with nothing to hope for. People who have moved on lie dead on the roads. I fear that when wheat should be sown, seed cannot be planted.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region most land is bare. Refugees lie dead on the roads. I fear that when wheat should be sown, seed cannot be planted.

sentences.zh: 宜詔在所裁留經用，以種貸民。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order each locality to set aside routine expenditures and lend seed to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Each locality should set aside routine expenditures and lend seed to the people.

sentences.zh: 今茲租賦及宿逋遠貸，一切蠲除。

translations.literal: This year's rents and levies, together with long-standing arrears and distant loans, should all be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: This year's rents and levies, with all old arrears and distant loans, should be remitted.

sentences.zh: 設不蠲除，亦無可斂之理，不如先事圖之，則恩歸於上。

translations.literal: Even if not remitted, there is no logic by which they can be collected. Better to plan ahead, and then the grace will belong to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Even if not remitted, they cannot be collected. Better to act first, and the credit will belong to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十四年夏旱，吏趣常賦，至縣令為民毆辱者，不可不察。」

translations.literal: In the summer drought of the fourteenth year, clerks urged regular taxes until district magistrates were beaten and humiliated by the people—this cannot go unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer drought of the fourteenth year, tax collectors pressed so hard that magistrates were beaten by the people. This cannot go unexamined.

sentences.zh: 又言：「漕運本濟關中，若轉東都以西緣道倉廩，悉入京師，督江、淮所輸以備常數，然後約太倉一歲計，斥其餘者以糶於民，則時價不踴而蓄藏者出矣。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Grand Canal transport was originally to supply Guanzhong. If the granaries along the route west of the Eastern Capital were all turned toward the capital, and the Yangzi-Huai deliveries supervised to meet regular quotas, then after reckoning the Grand Granary's yearly supply the surplus could be sold to the people—then market prices would not soar and hoarders would release their stores."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Canal transport was meant to supply Guanzhong. If route granaries west of the Eastern Capital fed the capital while Yangzi-Huai deliveries met regular quotas, surplus from the Grand Granary could be sold to the people. Prices would not soar and hoarders would release their stores."

sentences.zh: 又言：「大曆中，一縑直錢四千，今止八百，稅入如舊，則出於民者五倍其初。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the Dali era one bolt of silk was worth four thousand cash; now it is only eight hundred. If tax revenue remains as before, what is taken from the people is five times the original.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In the Dali era one bolt of silk was worth four thousand cash; now only eight hundred. If tax revenue stays the same, what is taken from the people is five times greater.

sentences.zh: 四方銳於上獻，為國掊怨，廣軍實之求，而兵有虛籍，剝取多方，雖有心計巧歷，能商功利，其於割股啖口，困人均也。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The four directions are keen to offer tribute upward, accumulating resentment for the state. Demands for military stores grow broad while army rolls contain empty names. Exactions come from many sides. However clever the accountants and however skilled at calculating profit, it is like cutting flesh to feed the mouth—the people are equally exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The regions compete in tribute, breeding resentment. Demands for military stores grow while army rolls hold empty names. Exactions come from every side. However clever the accountants, it is like cutting flesh to feed the mouth—the people are equally exhausted."

sentences.zh: 又言：「比經絀放者，自謂抆拭無期，坐為匪人，以動和氣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Those recently demoted and released, thinking they will never be wiped clean, sit as outcasts and disturb harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Those recently demoted, believing they will never be cleared, sit as outcasts and disturb public harmony.

sentences.zh: 而冬薦官逾三年未受命，衣食既空，溘然就斃，此亦窮人之一端也。

translations.literal: Winter-recommended officials who have gone more than three years without receiving appointment, their food and clothing exhausted, suddenly die—this too is one form of the people's desperation.
translations.idiomatic: Winter-recommended officials who wait more than three years without appointment, their food and clothing gone, suddenly die. This too is one face of desperation.

sentences.zh: 近陛下洗宥絀放者，或起為二千石，其徒更相勉，知牽復可望。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty pardoned demoted officials; some were raised to two-thousand-dan posts. Their fellows encouraged one another, knowing restoration could be hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Your Majesty pardoned demoted officials; some were raised to two-thousand-dan posts. Their fellows encouraged one another, knowing restoration was possible.

sentences.zh: 惟因而弘之，使人人自效。」

translations.literal: Only extend this further and let every man exert himself."
translations.idiomatic: Only extend this further and let every man exert himself."

sentences.zh: 帝頗采用之。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted these suggestions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely adopted these suggestions.

sentences.zh: 憲宗元和初，歷兵部侍郎，坐累，徙太子賓客，俄還前官。

translations.literal: Early in Xianzong's Yuanhe era he served as vice minister of war. On account of accumulated faults he was moved to mentor of the heir apparent, then soon restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianzong's Yuanhe era he served as vice minister of war. On account of accumulated faults he was moved to mentor of the heir apparent, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 時澤潞盧從史詐傲，浸不制，其父虔卒京師，而成德王承宗父死求襲，德輿諫，以為：「欲變山東，先擇昭義之帥。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Congshi of Zelu was deceitful and arrogant and gradually went unchecked. His father Qian died in the capital, and Wang Chengzong of Chengde sought succession when his father died. Deyu remonstrated, arguing: "To change Shandong, first choose a commander for Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi of Zelu was deceitful and arrogant and gradually went unchecked. His father Qian died in the capital while Wang Chengzong of Chengde sought succession. Deyu remonstrated: "To change Shandong, first choose a commander for Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 從史拔自軍校，偃蹇不法，今可因其喪，選守臣代之。

translations.literal: Congshi was plucked from army ranks and is arrogant and lawless. Now one can use his mourning to select a civil official to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi rose from the ranks and is arrogant and lawless. Use his mourning to replace him with a civil official.

sentences.zh: 成德習俗既久，當制以漸，許成德之請則可，許昭義則不可。」

translations.literal: Chengde's customs are long established and should be restrained gradually. Granting Chengde's request may be possible; granting Zhaoyi's request cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde's customs are long entrenched and should be changed gradually. Grant Chengde's request if you must, but not Zhaoyi's.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 及王承宗叛，從史乃詭計以撓王師，兵老無功。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Congshi then used deceitful schemes to impede the imperial army. The troops grew old and achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, Congshi used deceit to impede the imperial army. The campaign dragged on without success.

sentences.zh: 德輿復請赦承宗，徙從史。

translations.literal: Deyu again requested pardoning Chengzong and transferring Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu again asked to pardon Chengzong and transfer Congshi.

sentences.zh: 後皆略如所料。

translations.literal: Later events all roughly matched his prediction.
translations.idiomatic: Later events roughly matched his prediction.

sentences.zh: 會裴垍病，德輿自太常卿拜禮部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Pei Ji fell ill, Deyu was promoted from director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to minister of rites and concurrent chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji fell ill, Deyu was promoted from director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to minister of rites and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 王鍔繇河中入朝，求兼宰相，李藩以為不可，德輿亦奏：「平章事非序進宜得，比方鎮帶宰相，必有大忠若勛，否則強不制者，不得已與之。

translations.literal: Wang E came from Hezhong to court and requested to serve concurrently as chief minister. Li Fan thought this impossible. Deyu also memorialized: "Chief minister is not a rank one receives in ordinary promotion. When military commissioners are given the title, it must be for supreme loyalty and merit, or else for the uncontrollably powerful—given only when there is no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E came from Hezhong to court and asked to serve as chief minister. Li Fan objected. Deyu memorialized: "Chief minister is not an ordinary promotion. Military commissioners receive the title only for supreme loyalty and merit, or for the uncontrollably powerful when there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 今鍔無功，又非姑息時，一假此名，以開後人，不可。」

translations.literal: Now E has no merit, and this is not a time of indulgence. To lend him this title once would open the way for those who follow—it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: E has no merit, and this is not a time of indulgence. Granting the title once would open the door for others. It cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stopped.

sentences.zh: 董溪、于臯謨以運糧使盜軍興，流嶺南，帝悔其輕，詔中使半道殺之。

translations.literal: Dong Xi and Yu Gaomo, as grain transport commissioners, embezzled military funds and were exiled to Lingnan. The emperor regretted the lightness of the sentence and ordered palace envoys to kill them halfway.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi and Yu Gaomo, as grain transport commissioners, embezzled military funds and were exiled to Lingnan. The emperor regretted the light sentence and ordered palace envoys to kill them en route.

sentences.zh: 德輿諫：「溪等方山東用兵，乾沒庫財，死不償責。

translations.literal: Deyu remonstrated: "Xi and the others, during the Shandong campaign, embezzled treasury funds. Death does not repay the debt.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu remonstrated: "During the Shandong campaign Xi and the others embezzled treasury funds. Death does not repay the debt.

sentences.zh: 陛下以流斥太輕，當責臣等繆誤，審正其罪，明下詔書，與眾同棄，則人人懼法。
