translations.literal: Your Majesty considers exile too light. Then blame us ministers for our error, properly determine their crime, and clearly issue an edict casting them off with public consensus—then every man will fear the law.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty considers exile too light. Blame us ministers for our error, determine their crime properly, and issue a clear edict casting them off with public consensus. Then every man will fear the law.

sentences.zh: 臣知已事不諍，然異時或有此比，要須有司論報，罰一勸百，孰不甘心。」

translations.literal: I know that what is done cannot be disputed, yet at another time there may be similar cases. There must be discussion and reporting by the proper offices. Punish one to warn a hundred—who would not submit in heart?
translations.idiomatic: I know what is done cannot be undone, yet similar cases may arise. The proper offices must discuss and report. Punish one to warn a hundred—who would not submit?

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘗問政之寬猛孰先，對曰：「唐家承隋苛虐，以仁厚為先。

translations.literal: Once asked whether leniency or severity in governance should come first, he replied: "The Tang house succeeded Sui's harsh cruelty and takes benevolence and generosity first.
translations.idiomatic: Asked whether leniency or severity should come first in governance, he replied: "The Tang succeeded Sui's harsh cruelty and puts benevolence first.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝見《明堂圖》，始禁鞭背，列聖所循，皆尚德教。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong saw the Hall of Enlightenment diagram, he first forbade flogging the back. The successive sages have followed this and all honor moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong saw the Hall of Enlightenment diagram, he first forbade flogging the back. Successive emperors have honored moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 故天寶大盜竊發，俄而夷滅，蓋本朝之化，感人心之深也。」

translations.literal: Thus when the great rebellion erupted in Tianbao it was quickly extinguished—because this dynasty's transformation moves people's hearts so deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the great rebellion erupted in Tianbao it was quickly crushed—because this dynasty's moral influence runs so deep.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠如公言。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Truly as you say."

sentences.zh: 德輿善辨論，開陳古今本末，以覺悟人主。

translations.literal: Deyu was skilled at debate and exposition, setting forth the roots and branches of past and present to awaken the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was skilled at debate, setting forth past and present from root to branch to awaken the ruler.

sentences.zh: 為輔相，寬和不為察察名。

translations.literal: As chief minister he was lenient and harmonious and did not make a show of scrutinizing others' reputations.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was lenient and harmonious and did not nitpick reputations.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫再秉政，帝又自用李絳參贊大機。

translations.literal: Li Jifu again held power, and the emperor also relied on Li Jiang to assist in major decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu again held power, and the emperor also relied on Li Jiang for major decisions.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝切於治，事巨細悉責宰相。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was keen on governance and held the chief ministers responsible for matters great and small.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was keen on governance and held chief ministers responsible for everything.

sentences.zh: 吉甫、絳議論不能無持異，至帝前遽言亟辯，德輿從容不敢有所輕重，坐是罷為本官。

translations.literal: Jifu and Jiang in debate could not avoid holding differing views. Before the emperor they spoke hastily and argued urgently. Deyu was calm and did not dare weigh one side against the other. On this account he was dismissed to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu and Jiang could not avoid differing in debate and argued urgently before the emperor. Deyu stayed calm and would not take sides. For this he was dismissed to his original post.

sentences.zh: 以檢校吏部尚書留守東都，進扶風郡公。

translations.literal: He was made acting minister of personnel, left to guard the Eastern Capital, and advanced to Duke of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting minister of personnel, left to guard the Eastern Capital, and advanced to duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 于頔以子殺人，自囚，親戚莫敢過門，朝廷無為請者。

translations.literal: Yu Di, because his son murdered someone, imprisoned himself. Relatives dared not pass his gate, and at court no one pleaded for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di, because his son had murdered someone, imprisoned himself. Relatives dared not visit, and no one at court pleaded for him.

sentences.zh: 德輿將行，言於帝曰：「頔之罪既貸不竟，宜因賜寬詔。」

translations.literal: As Deyu was about to depart, he said to the emperor: "Yu's crime has already been pardoned though not yet resolved. It is fitting to grant him a lenient edict on this occasion.
translations.idiomatic: As Deyu was about to leave, he told the emperor: "Yu's crime has been pardoned but not fully resolved. You should grant him a lenient edict now.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然，卿為吾過諭之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is. Go and explain this to him on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Good. Go explain this to him for me."

sentences.zh: 復拜太常卿，徙刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was again appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔許孟容、蔣乂刊匯格敕，既成，上之，留禁中；

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had authorized Meng Rong and Jiang Yi to compile and edit regulations and edicts. When finished they submitted them, and they were kept within the Forbidden City;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Meng Rong and Jiang Yi had been ordered to compile regulations and edicts. When finished, the work was submitted and kept in the palace;

sentences.zh: 德輿請出其書，與侍郎劉伯芻參復研考，定三十篇奏上。

translations.literal: Deyu requested that the book be brought out. Together with Vice Minister Liu Bochu he reviewed and studied it again, fixed it in thirty sections, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu asked that the book be brought out. With Vice Minister Liu Bochu he reviewed it again, settled it in thirty sections, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 復檢校吏部尚書，出為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: He was again made acting minister of personnel and sent out as military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made acting minister of personnel and sent out as military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 後二年，以病乞還，卒於道。

translations.literal: Two years later, ill, he begged to return and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, ill, he begged to return and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 年六十，贈尚書左僕射，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He was sixty. Posthumously granted left vice director of the Department of State Affairs; posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty. Posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 德輿生三歲，知變四聲，四歲能賦詩，積思經術，無不貫綜。

translations.literal: Deyu at three knew the four tones in variation; at four could compose poetry. He accumulated thought on the classics—there was nothing he did not master comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: At three Deyu knew the four tones in variation; at four he could compose poetry. He mastered every branch of classical learning.

sentences.zh: 自始學至老，未曾一日去書不觀。

translations.literal: From first study to old age he never went a day without books before him.
translations.idiomatic: From first study to old age he never went a day without reading.

sentences.zh: 嘗著論，辨漢所以亡，西京以張禹，東京以胡廣，大指有補於世。

translations.literal: He once wrote a treatise analyzing why Han perished: the Western Capital through Zhang Yu, the Eastern Capital through Hu Guang. Its main points benefited the age.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a treatise on why Han fell, blaming Zhang Yu for the Western Capital and Hu Guang for the Eastern. Its main points served the age well.

sentences.zh: 其文雅正贍縟，當時公卿侯王功德卓異者，皆所銘紀，十常七八。

translations.literal: His literary style was elegant, upright, rich, and ornate. Of the chief ministers, dukes, and princes of the time whose merit and virtue were outstanding, seven or eight out of ten were inscribed by him.
translations.idiomatic: His style was elegant, upright, and rich. Seven or eight of every ten outstanding ministers, dukes, and princes had inscriptions from his hand.

sentences.zh: 雖動止無外飾，其醞藉風流，自然可慕。

translations.literal: Though in conduct and bearing he had no outward ornament, his cultured reserve and grace were naturally admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Though he wore no outward ornament, his cultured reserve and grace were naturally admirable.

sentences.zh: 貞元、元和間，為搢紳羽儀雲。

translations.literal: Between Zhenyuan and Yuanhe he was the standard for the gentry and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhenyuan and Yuanhe he was the model for the gentry and officials.

sentences.zh: 子 璩子璩，字大圭，元和初，擢進士。

translations.literal: His son was Ju. Ju, courtesy name Dagui—in the early Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ju, styled Dagui, passed the jinshi examination early in the Yuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 歷監察御史，有美稱。

translations.literal: He served as surveillance censor and had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He served as surveillance censor and won a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 宰相李宗閔乃父門生，故薦為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Zongmin had been his father's student; therefore he recommended him as secretariat drafting attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Zongmin had been his father's student and recommended him as secretariat drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 時李訓挾寵，以《周易》博士在翰林，璩與舍人高元裕、給事中鄭肅、韓佽等連章劾訓傾覆陰巧，且亂國，不宜出入禁中。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xun, relying on favor, served as Book of Changes doctor in the Hanlin Academy. Ju together with Attendant Gao Yuanyu, Drafting Secretary Zheng Su, Han Yi and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Xun for subversion and secret cunning, and for disturbing the state—unfit to enter and leave the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, relying on favor, served as Book of Changes doctor in the Hanlin Academy. Ju, Gao Yuanyu, Zheng Su, Han Yi, and others jointly impeached Xun for subversion and secret cunning, saying he was unfit to enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: (The emperor) did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 及宗閔貶，璩屢表辨解，貶閬州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zongmin was demoted, Ju repeatedly submitted memorials in his defense and was demoted to governor of Lang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongmin was demoted, Ju repeatedly defended him in memorials and was demoted to governor of Lang.

sentences.zh: 文宗憐其母病，徙鄭州。

translations.literal: Wenzong, pitying his mother's illness, transferred him to Zheng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, pitying his mother's illness, transferred him to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 訓誅，時人多璩明禍福大體，能世其家。

translations.literal: When Xun was executed, many of the time praised Ju for understanding the larger pattern of fortune and disaster and for being able to continue his family's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was executed, many praised Ju for seeing the larger pattern of fortune and disaster and continuing his family's tradition.

sentences.zh: 崔群

translations.literal: = Cui Qun =
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun

sentences.zh: 崔群，字敦詩，貝州武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Qun, courtesy name Dunshi, a man of Wucheng in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun, styled Dunshi, was from Wucheng in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 未冠，舉進士，陸贄主貢舉，梁肅薦其有公輔才，擢甲科，舉賢良方正，授秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: Before cap age he competed for jinshi. Lu Zhi supervised the examination; Liang Su recommended him as having talent for chief minister and aide. He was ranked in the top tier, passed the eminent and upright examination, and was appointed collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he took the jinshi exam under Lu Zhi. Liang Su recommended him as chief-minister material. He ranked first, passed the eminent and upright exam, and became a secretariat collator.

sentences.zh: 累遷右補闕、翰林學士、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to right remonstrance censor, Hanlin academician, and secretariat drafting attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right remonstrance censor, Hanlin academician, and secretariat drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 數陳讜言，憲宗嘉納，因詔學士：「凡奏議，待群署乃得上。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted candid words. Xianzong approved and accepted them. Thereupon an edict to the academicians: "All memorials and proposals must wait for Qun's signature before submission.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly offered candid counsel, which Xianzong welcomed. An edict then required all academy memorials to await Qun's signature.

sentences.zh: 群以「禁密之言，人人當自陳，一為故事，後或有惡直鬼正，則它學士不得上言矣」，固讓，見聽。

translations.literal: Qun argued: "Forbidden and secret words—every man should state them for himself. Once this becomes precedent, later there may be those who hate the straight and fear the upright, and then other academicians will not be able to speak up." He firmly declined and was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qun objected: "Secret matters should be reported by each man himself. Once this becomes precedent, those who hate the straight may block other academicians from speaking." He firmly declined and was heeded.

sentences.zh: 惠昭太子薨，是時，遂王嫡，而澧王長，多內助。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Huizhao died, at that time the Prince of Sui was the legitimate son, but the Prince of Li was older and had many inner supporters.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Huizhao died, the Prince of Sui was the legitimate son, but the older Prince of Li had many palace supporters.

sentences.zh: 帝將建東宮，詔群為澧王作讓。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to establish the Eastern Palace and ordered Qun to compose a declination for the Prince of Li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to establish the Eastern Palace and ordered Qun to compose a declination for the Prince of Li.

sentences.zh: 群奏：「大凡己當得則讓，不當得之，烏用讓？

translations.literal: Qun submitted: "Generally one yields when one ought to receive—when one ought not to receive, what use is yielding?
translations.idiomatic: Qun submitted: "One yields when one ought to receive. When one ought not to receive, what use is yielding?

sentences.zh: 今遂王嫡，宜為太子。」

translations.literal: Now the Prince of Sui is the legitimate son—he should be crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Sui is the legitimate son and should be crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 魏博田季安以五千縑助營開業佛祠，群以為無名之獻，不當受。

translations.literal: Tian Ji'an of Weibo offered five thousand bolts of silk to help build the Kaiye Buddhist temple. Qun held this an unsolicited gift and that it should not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ji'an of Weibo offered five thousand bolts of silk to build the Kaiye Buddhist temple. Qun held this an unsolicited gift and said it should be refused.

sentences.zh: 有詔卻之。

translations.literal: An edict declined it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declined it.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe he was made vice director of the secretariat and concurrent chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 12 he was made vice grand secretary and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 李師道既誅，師古等妻子沒入掖廷，帝疑，以問群，群請釋之，並還其奴婢貲產。

translations.literal: After Li Shidao was executed, Shigu and others' wives and children were seized into the palace women's quarters. The emperor was uncertain and asked Qun. Qun requested their release and return of their servants, assets, and property.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao was executed, Shigu's family was seized for the palace. The emperor asked Qun, who requested their release and the return of their servants and property.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵院官權長孺坐罪抵死，其母耄，丐子以養。

translations.literal: Quan Changru, an official of the Salt and Iron Commission, was convicted and faced death. His mother was very old and begged for her son to support her.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Changru of the Salt and Iron Commission was convicted and faced death. His aged mother begged for her son to support her.

sentences.zh: 帝奭然欲赦之，以問宰相，群對：「陛下幸憐其老，宜即遣使諭旨，若須出敕，無及矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor, suddenly moved, wished to pardon him and asked the chief ministers. Qun replied: "Your Majesty, pitying her age, should immediately send an envoy to announce your intent. If an edict must be issued, it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the emperor wished to pardon him and asked the chief ministers. Qun replied: "If Your Majesty pities her age, send an envoy at once. If you wait for an edict, it will be too late.

sentences.zh: 於是免死。

translations.literal: Thereupon death was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Death was remitted.

sentences.zh: 群凡啟奏，平恕如此。

translations.literal: In all Qun's submissions his fairness and leniency were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's memorials were always fair and lenient like this.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗語宰相：「聽受之際，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: The emperor once said to the chief ministers: "In hearing and accepting— is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told the chief ministers: "Hearing and judging cases—is it not difficult!

sentences.zh: 比詔學士集前世事，為《辨謗略》，以自儆鑒。

translations.literal: Recently I ordered the academicians to gather affairs of former ages and compile An Outline for Distinguishing Slander, to warn myself.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I ordered the academicians to gather past cases into An Outline for Distinguishing Slander, to warn myself.

sentences.zh: 其要云何？」

translations.literal: What is its essential point?
translations.idiomatic: What is its essential point?

sentences.zh: 群對：「無情，曲直辨之至易；

translations.literal: Qun replied: "When there is no personal feeling, right and wrong are easiest to distinguish;
translations.idiomatic: Qun replied: "Without personal feeling, right and wrong are easiest to distinguish;

sentences.zh: 有情，則欺為難審也。

translations.literal: when there is personal feeling, then deception is hard to examine.
translations.idiomatic: with personal feeling, deception is hard to examine.

sentences.zh: 故孔子有眾好眾惡、浸潤膚受之說，以其難辨也。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius spoke of popular favor and popular hatred, of things that seep in and touch the skin—it is because they are hard to distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius spoke of popular favor and hatred and of slander that seeps in because such things are hard to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 若陛下擇賢而任，待之以誠，糾之以法，則人自歸正，而不敢以欺。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty selects the worthy and employs them, treats them with sincerity, and corrects them with law, then people will naturally return to what is right and will not dare to deceive."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty selects the worthy, treats them sincerely, and corrects them by law, people will return to what is right and not dare to deceive."

sentences.zh: 帝韙其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 處州刺史苗積進羨錢七百萬，群以受之失信天下，請還賜其州，以紓下戶之賦。

translations.literal: Miao Ji, governor of Chuzhou, offered seven million in surplus funds. Qun held that accepting it would lose trust throughout the realm. He requested returning it as a gift to the prefecture to ease the taxes of lower households.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Ji, governor of Chuzhou, offered seven million in surplus funds. Qun said accepting it would lose public trust and asked that it be returned to the prefecture to ease taxes on poor households.

sentences.zh: 是時，皇甫镈言利幸於帝，陰藉左右求宰相，群數言其佞邪不可用。

translations.literal: At the time Huangfu Bo, skillful at speaking of profit, won the emperor's favor and covertly relied on those around him to seek the chief ministership. Qun repeatedly said he was flatteringly wicked and unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo, skilled at speaking of profit, won the emperor's favor and covertly sought the chief ministership through palace contacts. Qun repeatedly said he was flatteringly wicked and unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 既入對，及開元、天寶事，群因推言其極曰：「安危在出令，存亡系所任。

translations.literal: Once in audience, touching on the Kaiyuan and Tianbao affairs, Qun thereupon extended the argument to its limit: "Safety and danger depend on what orders are issued; survival and ruin depend on whom is appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In audience, discussing Kaiyuan and Tianbao, Qun pushed the argument to its limit: "Safety and danger depend on what orders are issued; survival and ruin depend on whom is appointed.

sentences.zh: 昔玄宗少歷屯險，更民間疾苦，故初得姚崇、宋璟、盧懷慎輔以道德，蘇颋、李元纮孜孜守正，則開元為治。

translations.literal: Formerly Xuanzong in youth passed through hardship and danger and experienced the people's suffering. Thus at first, having Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Lu Huaishen assist him with moral virtue, and Su Ting and Li Yuanhong diligently uphold the upright, Kaiyuan became well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong in youth knew hardship and the people's suffering. With Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Lu Huaishen guiding him in virtue, and Su Ting and Li Yuanhong upholding the upright, Kaiyuan was well governed.

sentences.zh: 其後安於逸樂，遠正士，昵小人，故宇文融以言利進，李林甫、楊國忠怙寵朋邪，則天寶為亂。

translations.literal: Later, secure in ease and pleasure, distant from upright men and close to petty men, Yuwen Rong advanced through speaking of profit, and Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong relied on favor and formed wicked factions—then Tianbao became disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Later, secure in pleasure, distant from upright men and close to petty ones, Yuwen Rong rose through profit, and Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong relied on favor and formed wicked factions—then Tianbao fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以開元為法，以天寶為戒，社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would take Kaiyuan as model and Tianbao as warning—the blessing of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should take Kaiyuan as model and Tianbao as warning. That would bless the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 又言：「世謂祿山反，為治亂分時。

translations.literal: He also said: "The world says that when Lushan rebelled was when order and disorder were divided.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The world says order and disorder were divided when Lushan rebelled.

sentences.zh: 臣謂罷張九齡，相林甫，則治亂固已分矣。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that when Zhang Jiuling was dismissed and Li Linfu made chief minister, order and disorder were already divided."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that when Zhang Jiuling was dismissed and Li Linfu made chief minister, order and disorder were already divided."

sentences.zh: 左右為感動。

translations.literal: Those at his side were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Those present were moved.

sentences.zh: 群以是諷帝，故镈銜之。

translations.literal: Qun used this to admonish the emperor; therefore Bo harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Qun used this to admonish the emperor, and Bo resented him.

sentences.zh: 帝卒自相镈。

translations.literal: The emperor in the end made Bo chief minister himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in the end made Bo chief minister.

sentences.zh: 會群臣上帝號，镈欲兼用「孝德」為號，群獨以為有「睿聖」，則「孝德」並見。

translations.literal: When the ministers presented a reign title to the emperor, Bo wished to include "Filial Virtue" in the title. Qun alone held that since "Sagely Wisdom" was already included, "Filial Virtue" would appear together with it.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers presented a reign title, Bo wanted to include Filial Virtue. Qun alone objected that Sagely Wisdom was already included.

sentences.zh: 帝聞不樂。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會度支稟賜邊士不時，物多弊惡，李光顏憂甚，至欲引佩刀自決，中外皆恐。

translations.literal: It happened that the treasury's grants to frontier soldiers were not timely and the goods were mostly shoddy and rotten. Li Guangyan was deeply troubled, even wishing to draw his sword and take his own life. Court and countryside were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury grants to frontier soldiers were late and the goods shoddy. Li Guangyan was so anguished he nearly killed himself. Court and countryside were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 镈奏：「邊鄙無事，乃群鼓動，欲以買直，歸怨天子。」

translations.literal: Bo memorialized: "The frontier is without incident—Qun is stirring up trouble, wishing to buy upright reputation and shift blame to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Bo memorialized: "The frontier is quiet. Qun is stirring trouble to buy a reputation for integrity and shift blame to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是罷為湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qun was dismissed and made observation commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qun was dismissed and made observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，以吏部侍郎召之，勞曰：「我為太子，卿力也。」

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, Qun was summoned as vice minister of personnel. The emperor comforted him, saying: "That I am crown prince—your effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Qun was summoned as vice minister of personnel. The emperor said: "I owe my position as crown prince to you.

sentences.zh: 群曰：「此先帝意，臣何力焉？

translations.literal: Qun said: "This was the late emperor's intent—what effort did your subject have?
translations.idiomatic: Qun said: "That was the late emperor's intent. What effort did I have?

sentences.zh: 且陛下向為淮西節度使，臣起制草，其言有『能辨南陽之牘，允符東海之貴』，先帝然之，則傳付久矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty was military governor of Huaixi, your subject drafted the edict. Its words included 'able to judge the documents of Nanyang, truly matching the worth of the Eastern Sea.' The late emperor approved it—then the succession was long since decided."
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was military governor of Huaixi, I drafted the edict with the words 'able to judge the documents of Nanyang, truly matching the worth of the Eastern Sea.' The late emperor approved it long ago."

sentences.zh: 俄拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校兵部尚書，充武寧節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting minister of war and military governor of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting minister of war and military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 群以其副王智興得士心，不若假以節度，不報。

translations.literal: Qun, because his deputy Wang Zhixing had won the soldiers' hearts, suggested granting him the military governorship. No response.
translations.idiomatic: Qun, seeing that his deputy Wang Zhixing had won the soldiers' hearts, suggested granting him the military governorship. There was no response.

sentences.zh: 智興討幽、鎮還，藉兵逐群，群失守，左遷秘書監，分司東都。

translations.literal: Zhixing returned from campaigning against You and Zhen, used his troops to drive Qun out. Qun lost his post and was demoted to director of the secretariat, assigned to the Eastern Capital branch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing returned from campaigning against You and Zhen, used his troops to drive Qun out, and Qun was demoted to director of the secretariat at the Eastern Capital branch.

sentences.zh: 改華州刺史，歷宣歙池觀察使，進兵部尚書，出為荊南節度使，召拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to governor of Hua, served as observation commissioner of Xuan-Xi-Chi, advanced to minister of war, sent out as military governor of Jingnan, and recalled as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Hua, served as observation commissioner of Xuan-Xi-Chi, rose to minister of war, was sent out as military governor of Jingnan, and was recalled as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-one and was posthumously granted minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：聖人不畏多難，畏無難。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The sage does not fear many difficulties—he fears no difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The sage does not fear many difficulties—he fears no difficulty.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 多難之世，人人長慮而深謀，日惕於中，猶以為未也，曰：「吾覆亡不暇，又何以安？」

translations.literal: In an age of many difficulties, every man plans long and thinks deep, daily vigilant within, yet still thinks it insufficient, saying: "I have no leisure before ruin—how can I be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: In an age of many difficulties, every man plans long and thinks deep, daily vigilant within, yet still thinks it insufficient, saying: "I have no leisure before ruin—how can I be at ease?

sentences.zh: 故能舉天下付之興，畏之也。

translations.literal: Thus he can entrust all under Heaven to rise—through fear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he can entrust the realm to rise—through fear.

sentences.zh: 禍難已平，上恬下嬉，施施自如曰：「賢難得，雖無賢，尚可治也；

translations.literal: When calamity is already pacified, superiors are at ease and inferiors play, strolling freely and saying: "The worthy are hard to find. Even without the worthy, the realm can still be governed;
translations.idiomatic: When calamity is pacified, superiors grow complacent and inferiors play, saying easily: "The worthy are hard to find. Even without them the realm can still be governed;

sentences.zh: 佞可去，雖存佞，不遽亂也。」

translations.literal: the flatterer can be removed. Even if flatterers remain, disorder does not come at once.
translations.idiomatic: flatterers can be removed. Even if some remain, disorder does not come at once.

sentences.zh: 視漏弗填，忽傾弗支，偃然自慰曰：「我曷以喪？」

translations.literal: Seeing the leak and not filling it, suddenly tilted and not supporting, lying at ease and comforting oneself: "How could I perish?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the leak and not filling it, suddenly tilted and unsupported, lying at ease and saying: "How could I perish?"

sentences.zh: 故能舉天下付之亡，不畏也。

translations.literal: Thus he can entrust all under Heaven to ruin—through lack of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he can entrust the realm to ruin—through lack of fear.

sentences.zh: 常人所畏，聖人易之；

translations.literal: What ordinary men fear, the sage treats lightly;
translations.idiomatic: What ordinary men fear, the sage treats lightly;

sentences.zh: 所不畏，聖人難之。

translations.literal: what they do not fear, the sage finds difficult.
translations.idiomatic: what they do not fear, the sage finds difficult.

sentences.zh: 觀孝明皇帝，本中主，遭變可與謀始，持成不可與共終。

translations.literal: Consider Emperor Xiaoming—originally a middling ruler. Encountering change, one could plan the beginning with him; holding achievement, one could not see the end through with him.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Emperor Xiaoming—a middling ruler. One could plan the beginning with him in crisis, but not see success through to the end.

sentences.zh: 崔群以為相李林甫則治亂已分，其言信哉！

translations.literal: Cui Qun held that making Li Linfu chief minister already divided order and disorder. How true his words!
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qun held that making Li Linfu chief minister already divided order and disorder. How true his words!

sentences.zh: 是扁鵲所以誚桓侯也。

translations.literal: This is why Bian Que reproached Duke Huan of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Bian Que reproached Duke Huan of Cai.
